title: FBI offers $5,000 reward for wanted Nigerian woman
summary: The FBI is offering up to $5,000 for information leading to Emuobosan Emanuella Hall’s arrest. She failed to report to prison to begin an eight-year sentence.
body:
The FBI is offering a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to the arrest of Emuobosan Emanuella Hall, who failed to report to a federal prison to begin serving an eight-year sentence. Hall, 46, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering and conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud. She was sentenced to 96 months in prison in January 2026.

Hall was charged in 2024 over her role in a romance scam and was arrested in Georgia before being released on bond. The FBI says she did not appear at the facility where she was ordered to serve her sentence in March 2026. A federal arrest warrant was issued on March 31, and she was later charged with failing to appear for service of a sentence and indicted on that charge.

According to the US Department of Justice, people involved in the scheme approached victims on social media, presenting themselves as generals, philanthropists or entrepreneurs based outside the United States. After forming romantic relationships, they persuaded victims to send money under false pretences, including claims that funds were needed for charity or sick relatives. Hall and co-defendant Kenneth G. Akpieyi used Le Beau Monde LLC to handle money from victims. Hall admitted responsibility for $851,207 in losses. Akpieyi was held responsible for more than $3.5 million in losses and sentenced to 25 years in prison in 2025.

The FBI said Hall’s electronic monitoring device last transmitted from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on March 24, 2026. She had told her probation officer she planned to travel to Minnesota, where she was expected to serve her sentence, but airline records showed she did not board the scheduled flight. Hall was born in Nigeria and is also known as Emuobosan E. Hall, Emuobosan Emanuella Erih and “Mobo.” If convicted of failing to report, she could face up to 10 additional years in prison, served consecutively to her existing sentence, and a fine of up to $250,000. The FBI is asking anyone with information about her whereabouts to contact the agency.

title: Shooting At California Halloween Store Kills One, Wounds Six
summary: One person was killed and six wounded in a shooting at a Halloween store in Fairfield, California. Police said investigators had not identified a suspect.
body:
One person was killed and six others were wounded in a shooting Friday evening at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, northern California, police said. The shooting took place shortly before 8:30 p.m. at the store in the Solano Town Center mall, about 47 miles northeast of San Francisco.

Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall said the six people wounded by gunfire were taken to hospital. At least three were in critical condition. Police had not identified the person or people responsible, and Marshall said the crime scene and investigation remained active late Friday.

The shooting occurred hours before Halloween, which was being celebrated in the United States on Saturday. Marshall said areas outside the mall were not under lockdown.

title: ‘Debt worse than leprosy’ – Obasanjo tackles Tinubu
summary: Olusegun Obasanjo said public debt could burden future generations, challenging President Bola Tinubu’s defence of borrowing. He also warned Africa against foreign control of AI.
body:
‘Debt worse than leprosy’ – Obasanjo tackles Tinubu

Former President Olusegun Obasanjo criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, saying accumulated debt could burden generations to come. Speaking Friday at a public forum in Abeokuta, Ogun State, he argued that debt’s effects extend beyond individuals and can mortgage a country’s future. Tinubu said in April that borrowing was not inherently wrong if Nigeria could repay it. The debate comes amid concerns over the country’s rising debt and the share of government revenue used for servicing it.

Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic record, citing the naira’s decline against the US dollar. He recalled that when he established his farm 47 years ago, one naira was worth $1.85, and contrasted that with a rate of 1,500 naira to the dollar. He urged political leaders to show they understand the country’s problems and can identify practical responses. He also said Nigeria should scrutinise prescriptions from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund rather than assume they suit the country’s circumstances.

On artificial intelligence, Obasanjo warned that African countries could face a new form of external exploitation if foreign interests control the technology. Though he said he lacked technical expertise in AI, he argued that technologies beyond a country’s control could be used against it. He urged leaders to examine what technology transfer means and whether its terms serve African interests. Obasanjo also pointed to the estimated 24 million Nigerian children out of school and called for AI to help improve access to education. In agriculture, he said the technology could help farmers select suitable crops, raise productivity and support food security.

Historian Umar Ardo, the event’s guest speaker, warned that AI could deepen inequality if African countries remain dependent on foreign technology firms. He called for stronger protection of data and traditional knowledge, domestic computing and energy capacity, investment in local AI research, and models suited to African languages and practices. Ardo also urged governments to direct AI applications towards services such as primary healthcare and agricultural support, and called for cooperation among African countries on data rules and shared infrastructure. He said the continent should seek ownership and a fair share of the value generated from its data, rather than remain a consumer of technology developed elsewhere.

title: Airtel Nigeria rolls out Open Network initiative to address service quality issues
summary: Airtel Nigeria has launched an app feature showing nearby network sites and their status. Subscribers can report service problems for technical teams to assess.
body:
Airtel Nigeria has launched an Open Network feature in the MyAirtel app, allowing subscribers to view nearby network sites, check their status and report service problems. The company says location-specific feedback will help it investigate issues and direct network improvements to areas where they are most needed.

Announced in Lagos on Friday by Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Dinesh Balsingh, the initiative is intended to give customers more visibility into Airtel’s network and a digital channel for describing their experiences. Balsingh said the information could help technical teams pinpoint where service challenges occur, as Nigerians increasingly rely on mobile connectivity for business, education and communication.

Subscribers can find Open Network in the app’s Quick Actions section. The feature may request location access to display nearby sites. Its colour-coded map marks active sites serving locations in red, active sites undergoing upgrades in blue, and planned sites that are not yet operational in black. Users can report poor voice-call quality, slow or unavailable internet, and video buffering. Reports ask for the affected phone number and details including whether the issue occurs indoors or outdoors, how long it has lasted, and whether it is continuous or happens at particular times.

Nigerian Communications Commission Executive Vice Chairman Aminu Maida welcomed the initiative as consistent with the regulator’s focus on transparency and consumer empowerment. He said better access to network information could help connect operators’ infrastructure investments with customers’ expectations, while cautioning that a nearby site does not guarantee reliable service or faster internet. Congestion, transmission constraints and other technical factors can also affect performance.

The launch comes amid continued concerns about telecommunications service quality. Last week, the House of Representatives directed telecom company chief executives to appear before it to address the persistent decline in service, warning of possible arrest for non-compliance. Operators reportedly invested more than N2.5 trillion in network infrastructure in 2025, while fibre cuts and equipment vandalism remain challenges.

title: Tennis: Fernandez beats Rakhimova to reach Tokyo final
summary: Leylah Fernandez beat Kamilla Rakhimova 7-5, 6-3 in Tokyo to reach the Pan Pacific Open final. She will face Diana Shnaider or Mia Pohankova.
body:
Canada’s Leylah Fernandez advanced to the Pan Pacific Open final in Tokyo on Saturday, defeating Uzbekistan’s Kamilla Rakhimova 7-5, 6-3. The world number 23 secured the win in just under two hours, hitting nine aces and recovering from an early break in each set.

Rakhimova, ranked 66th, had lost in qualifying but entered the main draw as a lucky loser and reached the semi-finals. She was seeking her first WTA Tour final. Fernandez responded after falling behind in both sets, breaking back and taking control of the match.

Fernandez will play either Russia’s Diana Shnaider or Slovakia’s Mia Pohankova in the final as she pursues her seventh WTA Tour title. Her run in Tokyo continues a strong stretch in Asia: she won her first title of the season in Singapore last month, then reached the final of the Ningbo Open in China last week, where she lost to Elena Rybakina.

Fernandez reached the Tokyo quarter-finals after Rybakina withdrew from their scheduled match with a neck injury. Rybakina had secured the year-end world number one ranking a day earlier.

title: US, S.Korea, Japan Vow ‘Complete’ N.Korea Denuclearisation
summary: U.S., South Korean and Japanese officials renewed their commitment to North Korea’s complete denuclearization. They also backed full enforcement of U.N. sanctions.
body:
The United States, South Korea and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea during talks on Friday in Atlanta, held on the sidelines of a Group of 20 meeting. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi also pledged to fully implement U.N. Security Council resolutions, including measures barring support for revenue used in North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

The discussions come amid speculation about a possible meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China. Trump has repeatedly expressed interest in nuclear talks with Pyongyang. Last year, he described North Korea as “sort of a nuclear power” and said he was “100 percent” open to meeting Kim, but the suggestion received no response. The United States has also scaled back joint military drills with South Korea.

North Korea has rejected disarmament and declared its nuclear arsenal permanent and irreversible, while enshrining its status as a nuclear-armed state in law. Despite long-running U.N. sanctions, the country continues to pursue its nuclear and missile programmes and is backed by Russia and China. On Saturday, Pyongyang condemned a joint statement from countries monitoring sanctions enforcement, saying sanctions could not change its position as a nuclear weapons state.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, who has offered talks without preconditions, suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze on North Korea’s nuclear programme rather than immediate elimination, in exchange for sanctions relief. Critics argue that such a deal could amount to accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while easing pressure without requiring it to give up its weapons. Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency have also said Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on possible talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong.

title: Five key lessons from Nigeria Health Watch’s 2026 Health Conference
summary: At Nigeria’s 2026 health conference, experts said innovation must deliver accessible, lasting care. They highlighted reliable data, community input, trained workers and outbreak readiness.
body:
The 11th annual Future of Health Conference brought together policymakers, researchers, health professionals, innovators, development partners and private-sector representatives to discuss how Nigeria can strengthen its health system. A central theme was moving beyond promising pilots and isolated successes to solutions that reach more people and improve health outcomes over time.

The discussions stressed that innovation should be judged by its practical impact, not simply by whether a new technology has been developed. Devices and interventions need to be affordable and accessible, and supported by financing, infrastructure and trained workers. A diagnostic tool, for example, has limited value if no one can operate it or patients cannot access appropriate follow-up care.

Reliable data was another priority. A presentation on Nigeria’s HIV response described how a national survey revised the estimated number of people living with HIV from 3.2 million to 1.8 million, changing the reported treatment coverage figure. Researchers studying malaria drug resistance are also using molecular analysis to track patterns across locations. Conference discussions emphasised that such evidence must be clearly communicated and used in policy and health programmes.

Presentations highlighted the role of communities in shaping research and services. In the ENABLE study on Lassa fever, engagement helped researchers identify infections that might otherwise have gone undetected, including cases where symptoms such as tiredness were not initially considered serious. Maternal healthcare discussions made a related point about delivery systems: a Project HOPE-supported initiative in Bwari Area Council is working across 10 primary healthcare facilities, with five equipped as ultrasound hubs. The effort combines equipment with health worker training, mentorship, supervision and referrals, underscoring that technology alone cannot strengthen primary care.

The final lesson was that epidemic preparedness depends on work done before an outbreak. The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations’ 100 Days Mission aims to develop safe and effective vaccines against a new pandemic threat within 100 days of its identification, with initial authorisation and readiness for large-scale manufacturing as goals. It does not mean vaccinating entire populations within that period. Experts said sustained funding and partnerships among governments, researchers, philanthropic organisations and industry are needed to support preparedness and equitable access to health technologies.

title: [VIDEO] 2027: Hamzat Unveils Manifesto,100 Pledges For A More Prosperous Lagos
summary: Obafemi Hamzat unveiled a 100-pledge manifesto for Lagos, highlighting health care, transport, education, food costs and security. He said children are central to his plans.
body:
Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress candidate for Lagos State governor in the 2027 general elections, has unveiled a manifesto containing 100 pledges. Speaking at the launch at the Wole Soyinka Centre in Iganmu on Friday, the deputy governor said he would continue a progressive vision aimed at making Lagos more prosperous. He described children as central to his plans and said the commitments would be delivered.

Among the proposals, Hamzat pledged to add 580 hospital beds to expand access to health care. He also promised improvements to roads and transport, including activating the Fourth Mainland Bridge project. He said the state was pursuing a university of medicine to help young Nigerians pursue careers in the health sector.

The manifesto also includes plans to strengthen teacher development and review compensation for Lagos workers. Hamzat said his proposed administration would seek to reduce food costs from farm to table and equip young people with skills for current and future needs. Other pledges include cheaper broadband, improved security and more room to build.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu praised Hamzat’s record of public service at the event. He recalled that Hamzat set aside his own governorship ambition in 2018 in support of him, and said Lagos would experience a transition between administrations without rancour.

title: Organisers reveals how Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win
summary: Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe by 28 points to win the Ballon d’Or, the narrowest margin under the award’s current voting system. Kane received 40 first-place votes.
body:
Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d’Or by 28 points over Kylian Mbappe, the narrowest margin under the award’s current voting system. The voting breakdown, disclosed on Friday, showed Kane finished with 1,055 points, while Mbappe received 1,027.

Kane, the Bayern Munich and England forward, was ranked first by 40 of the 100 jurors. Mbappe, the France captain who plays for Real Madrid, received 23 first-place votes. Kane became the first Englishman to win the men’s award since Michael Owen in 2001.

The previous closest result under the current system was in 2024, when Rodri, then playing for Manchester City, beat Real Madrid’s Vinicius Junior by 41 points. The latest result was considerably tighter than last season’s: Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele earned 1,380 points and finished 321 ahead of Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal.

Yamal placed third in this year’s voting with 881 points, 174 behind Kane. The Ballon d’Or is decided by journalists, with one juror representing each of the top 100 nations in FIFA’s men’s rankings. For the women’s award, the voting panel represents the top 50 nations in the rankings.

title: Airlines’ annual payment processing cost hits $25bn
summary: Airlines spend more than $24.5bn a year processing payments, IATA says. It urged carriers to build financial processes into digital transformation.
body:
Airlines spend more than $24.5bn annually processing payments, according to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), which said the cost underscores the financial pressures facing carriers as they adopt digital technologies. Sandrine Le Borgne, IATA’s interim Director General, Chief Financial Officer and Senior Vice-President for Corporate Services, raised the issue at the opening of the association’s World Financial Symposium and World Passenger Symposium in Macao on Wednesday.

Le Borgne said airlines need to ensure that digital wallets, artificial intelligence and biometric identification do more than make travel more convenient. Their adoption should also reduce costs, simplify operations and support financial resilience. IATA said AI assistants and automated agents could change how passengers search for, compare and buy travel services, but carriers need to retain control of their data, commercial relationships and the information used to sell their services.

The association pointed to the Offers and Orders framework as a central part of the shift to modern airline retailing. Seven airlines are already using or implementing Orders, and more than 20 others are expected to follow from 2027. Technology providers have committed more than $1.7bn to Offers and Orders, IATA said, describing the framework as a basis for retailing that AI could help accelerate.

IATA also urged airlines to include reconciliation, settlement and revenue accounting in digital transformation from the outset, rather than simply converting existing processes to digital formats. New payment methods may give customers more choice, but they can also affect transaction costs, cash flow and financial risk, the association said.

Biometrics and digital travel credentials could make airport procedures faster and more convenient, but IATA said their benefits are constrained because many systems operate only within particular airports or countries. That fragmentation can prevent passengers from having a consistent experience across international journeys.

title: Süper Lig: Osimhen scores again as Galatasaray thrash Konyaspor
summary: Victor Osimhen scored as Galatasaray beat Konyaspor 4-0, moving to 22 points after 10 league matches. Chidozie Awaziem played the full game for the hosts.
body:
Victor Osimhen scored again as Galatasaray defeated Konyaspor 4-0 on Friday to strengthen their hold on top spot in the Turkish Süper Lig. The win took Okan Buruk’s side to 22 points after 10 matches, with Osimhen’s goal his ninth in eight league appearances this season.

The Nigerian striker opened the scoring in the 12th minute, heading in Gabriel Sara’s free kick. He nearly added another in first-half stoppage time, but his attempt from the left side of the penalty area was tipped over the crossbar. Yunus Akgün made it 2-0 in the 28th minute, finishing from outside the box after a corner worked by Sara and Batrakov.

Galatasaray extended their lead soon after the break when Aleksey Batrakov collected Sara’s pass inside the area and scored in the 49th minute, his first league goal for the club. Six minutes later, VAR overturned referee Cihan Aydın’s decision to award a corner following an incident involving Rafael Leão. Leão converted the resulting penalty to complete the scoring and register his first goal for Galatasaray.

Osimhen was substituted in the 61st minute after recording five shots, including three on target. The result was significant given Galatasaray had lost four of their previous six visits to Konyaspor, including a 2-0 defeat on their last trip. Konyaspor defender Chidozie Awaziem played the full match. He made two interceptions, three clearances and three recoveries, won three of four ground duels and completed 97 per cent of his passes.

Galatasaray have now won eight of their 10 league matches and are due to host VfB Stuttgart in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, 3 November.

title: BREAKING: OPay post-IPO trading halted after raising $304 million
summary: OPay’s NYSE debut was delayed after the company raised $304 million in its U.S. IPO. An exchange feed showed a news-pending halt, with no trades recorded.
body:
OPay’s shares did not begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange on Friday, October 30, as scheduled, despite the Nigeria-focused payments company having completed its $304 million U.S. initial public offering. An exchange message feed displayed a halt with news pending, and showed no executed trades. The reason for the halt and a new start time for trading were not stated.

The offering comprised 16 million American depositary shares, priced at $19 each. That was the bottom of OPay’s previously announced range of $19 to $21 per share. As of 2 p.m. in New York on Friday, the shares were indicated to open between $16.25 and $16.75—below the IPO price. The offering had valued the digital financial services provider at approximately $4 billion.

The delay contrasts with earlier reports that trading had commenced. OPay had priced its IPO and held an opening-bell ceremony, but the shares had yet to trade, according to the latest account. The offering had been scheduled to begin on October 30 under the ticker OPAY.

The company has also proposed a secondary listing on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, which would follow completion of its primary U.S. listing. OPay’s board and shareholders had approved the proposal, intended to provide Nigerian investors with access to the company’s shares while it maintains its primary listing in the United States.

title: Three Killed In Kwara Road Crash
summary: Three people were reportedly killed when a passenger bus and a truck collided near Okolowo in Ilorin early Friday. An eyewitness said the crash sparked a fire.
body:
Three people were reportedly killed when a passenger bus and a truck collided near the Okolowo area of Ilorin, the Kwara State capital, in the early hours of Friday. The crash occurred near Ibrolak Filling Station.

The bus was reportedly carrying day-old chicks and travelling from Lagos towards northern Nigeria. The truck, which was loaded with sacks suspected to contain sawdust, was coming from the direction of Shao and attempted to make a U-turn towards Okolowo, according to the account of an eyewitness.

The eyewitness said the bus struck the truck and the impact triggered a fire that engulfed both vehicles. Three people were left burnt beyond recognition, the eyewitness said. The account also said Federal Road Safety Corps officials arrived early the following morning to evacuate the victims’ remains.

Kwara State FRSC Sector Commander Kabiru Babatunde Kazeem confirmed the accident when contacted on Friday. The supplied account did not provide further details about the victims or the circumstances of the collision.

title: Ebola: Abia sets up isolation centre — Otti
summary: Abia has designated an isolation centre at Umuahia’s Mother and Child Hospital as a precaution against Ebola, though no cases have been reported. The state says it is prepared.
body:
Abia State has activated precautionary measures against Ebola and designated an isolation centre at the recently renovated Mother and Child Hospital in Umuahia. Governor Alex Otti said the facility would not be opened for general public use and would be available if needed. The state has no reported Ebola cases, he said, urging residents to follow health protocols without panicking.

Otti announced the measures during his monthly media chat for October in Umuahia. He said the state had put response protocols in place and was prepared to act if a case emerged.

The governor also reported that 31,000 people had been screened through the Abia State Eye Health Management Bureau, with 1,811 patients receiving surgery. Of those operations, 304 were free cataract surgeries. Abia has established 25 eye centres across its 17 local government areas, and Otti said he had approved four more, bringing the planned total to 29.

On public transport, Otti said Abia had chosen electric vehicles rather than compressed natural gas (CNG) buses for its system. He said the state was not opposed to CNG, and that companies had shown interest in establishing refuelling stations for other users. He also used the media briefing to review his administration’s work in areas including roads, healthcare, power and utilities.

title: Zamfara is evidence of transformational leadership under Gov Lawal, says EFCC Chairman
summary: EFCC Chairman Olanipekun Olukoyede said Zamfara’s recent changes show transformational leadership under Governor Dauda Lawal. He spoke at the state’s 30th anniversary.
body:
EFCC Chairman Olanipekun Olukoyede described developments in Zamfara as evidence of transformational leadership under Governor Dauda Lawal. He delivered the keynote address at an anniversary lecture marking 30 years since the state’s creation, held at the Government House in Gusau.

Olukoyede said he had reviewed the state’s history and the governor’s work before accepting the invitation. He noted that his professional role rarely takes him to political events or government houses, and said he discussed his assessment of Zamfara with the president before travelling. He also said the anniversary marked his first visit to the state.

On arriving in Gusau, Olukoyede said he noticed the new airport, paved roads and solar street lighting. He described the changing appearance of the capital as a sign of wider change in the state. He also cited what he said was steady improvement in Zamfara’s performance in NECO and WAEC examinations, alongside expanding public infrastructure. The lecture’s theme was “accountability and responsibility in transformational government.”

Governor Lawal said the anniversary theme, “Reflections, Achievements, and the Future,” was intended to consider the challenges that have shaped Zamfara and the steps needed to improve its future. He said discussions at the event covered public accountability, community involvement in addressing insecurity, the preservation of history and culture, and connections between security and socio-economic development.

Lawal said the administration’s Six-Point Rescue Agenda addresses the state’s challenges, while the Zamfara State Development Plan 2025–2034 sets out longer-term priorities for the economy, infrastructure, social welfare, human capital, governance and environmental sustainability. Other speakers at the anniversary lecture included Professors Tijjani Muhammad Bande, Sulaiman Kura, Murtala Rufai and Taofik Aminu.

title: Hakimi bags hat-trick as Paris Saint-Germain rip Le Havre to pieces
summary: Achraf Hakimi scored a hat-trick as Paris Saint-Germain beat Le Havre 5-1. The win put PSG four points clear after nine Ligue 1 games.
body:
Achraf Hakimi scored three times as Paris Saint-Germain came from behind to beat Le Havre 5-1 on Friday. The result lifted the champions to 20 points after nine Ligue 1 matches and opened a four-point lead over nearest rivals Rennes, who lost 5-2 at Nice.

Le Havre, bottom of the table, took the lead in the 18th minute when Josh Maja struck against the run of play. PSG responded quickly: Mika Godts ran onto a through-ball from Hakimi to equalise in the 26th minute, and Hakimi put the visitors ahead two minutes later with a low shot inside the near post.

Hakimi extended PSG’s advantage with a free-kick that curled past goalkeeper Arnaud Bodard. After the hour, Senny Mayulu made it 4-1, finishing from distance on a break while Le Havre’s goalkeeper was well away from his line. Hakimi completed his hat-trick in the 69th minute, threading a shot through a crowded area. Coach Luis Enrique substituted him shortly after.

Luis Enrique rested Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves, while Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were unavailable through injury. PSG’s position at the top could still change: Lille could move within two points with a win over Lens later on Friday, and Monaco had the same opportunity ahead of their Sunday match at Paris FC.

title: Debt Worse Than Leprosy, Destroys Generations, Says Obasanjo
summary: Olusegun Obasanjo says borrowing can burden future generations, while Bola Tinubu argues loans will fund infrastructure and support economic growth.
body:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, saying debt can damage the prospects of future generations. Speaking at a symposium in Abeokuta, Ogun State, he described debt as worse than leprosy and called the view that borrowing is acceptable if loans can be repaid “absolute nonsense.” The forum focused on using artificial intelligence to address grassroots problems and accelerate national development.

Obasanjo also challenged Nigeria’s economic record, recalling that when he established his farm 47 years ago, one naira exchanged for $1.85. He asked the country’s leaders to account for the naira’s depreciation to about ₦1,500 to the dollar and questioned what had been achieved over the intervening decades.

Historian and public policy scholar Umar Ardo, the symposium’s guest speaker, warned that artificial intelligence could increase Africa’s reliance on foreign powers. He said the continent risked having the technology used to manage it rather than help it shape its future unless it invested in chip fabrication, data centres and African-owned datasets, and strengthened cooperation across the continent.

Tinubu has defended plans for further foreign borrowing, arguing that long-term infrastructure investment is needed to support his administration’s ambition of making Nigeria a $1 trillion economy by 2030. He said the proposed loans would fund roads, electricity improvements, port upgrades and other projects intended to create jobs and support businesses. Projects he listed included the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto-Badagry and Trans-Sahara superhighways, improvements to the electricity grid and upgrades to major commercial ports in Lagos.

The President projected that the Lagos-Calabar highway could cut transport costs along its route by 15 to 20 per cent and add up to two per cent to GDP through increased trade, tourism and industrial activity. He estimated it could generate about 100,000 direct construction and engineering jobs and more than 150,000 indirect jobs. The Nigeria Labour Congress has questioned the government’s request for parliamentary approval to borrow $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion, given claims that revenue has risen since the petrol subsidy was removed.

title: FG begins N50,000 monthly cash relief for vulnerable Nigerian households
summary: The Federal Government has begun monthly N50,000 payments to eligible vulnerable households under a new relief programme. Payments require no application or fee.
body:
The Federal Government has started a monthly cash relief programme providing N50,000 to eligible vulnerable households, according to Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction Minister Bernard Doro. In a statement issued in Abuja on October 30, 2026, Doro described the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) as a presidential initiative intended to help households manage rising living costs, including higher food prices and the cost of essential goods.

The payments are intended to help recipients meet essential needs. The programme will be reviewed periodically to reflect changes in living costs, and beneficiaries will be notified directly before any payment adjustments. The ministry is working with licensed digital financial service providers to deliver the funds securely and transparently.

Beneficiaries are expected to receive text messages from service providers seeking consent before payments are made into bank accounts or mobile wallets. Doro said people would not need to apply, pay a fee or register through an agent. He warned against sharing Personal Identification Numbers or Bank Verification Numbers, and advised anyone unsure about a message or asked for money to call the NERSI helpline at 0700-022-2222.

Doro said NERSI would complement existing federal social protection and economic support programmes, and linked it to the government’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Separately, the World Bank reported that the Federal Government had disbursed N658.9 billion in direct cash transfers to 10.46 million poor and vulnerable households by September 2026. The report said biometric and digital verification were used to identify recipients. It also said the impact of cash transfers would depend on extending coverage, improving payment adequacy and regularity, and building a more sustainable system with dedicated federal and state budget allocations and gradually increased government funding.

title: ‘There’s Pain In My Mind And Soul,’ Says US Woman Who Survived Botched Execution
summary: Christa Pike says she remains in physical and emotional pain a month after surviving a failed execution in Tennessee. Her lawyers are seeking a commutation.
body:
Christa Pike says she has been in constant pain since surviving a failed execution attempt at a Tennessee prison a month ago. In a statement released Friday by her lawyers, the 50-year-old described ongoing physical pain and difficulty speaking, as well as emotional distress. “There is pain in my mind and in my soul,” she said.

Pike received two doses of pentobarbital on September 30, but the usually fatal amount did not kill her. She was taken to hospital in critical condition, received medical treatment and later returned to prison. The Death Penalty Information Center says she is the only inmate known to have survived after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs.

Pike was sentenced to death for the killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp. Pike was 18 at the time; she and her boyfriend beat and killed Slemmer. Pike said she is recovering, while cautioning that healing does not mean she is okay. She said she does not know why she survived or what will happen next, and is trying to heal one day at a time.

Since the attempt, Pike’s lawyers have repeatedly asked Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to commute her sentence to life in prison. Lee has suspended executions in the state while an independent investigation is conducted. Asked about Pike’s fate this week, he said he expected her sentence to remain unchanged unless the courts determined otherwise.

There have been 32 executions in the United States this year, all by lethal injection. The death penalty has been abolished in 23 states, while California, Oregon and Pennsylvania have moratoriums in place.

title: Security threats: Army chief urges troops to remain vigilant
summary: Army chief Waidi Shaibu urged troops to remain alert and uphold professional standards as he inaugurated accommodation and welfare projects in Ibadan.
body:
Nigerian Army Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Waidi Shaibu has urged personnel to remain vigilant, disciplined and committed as they respond to changing security threats. He delivered the message on Thursday at the inauguration of projects at Adekunle Fajuyi and Letmauck Cantonments in Ibadan, Oyo State. Shaibu was represented at the event by Maj. Gen. Auwalu Mahmuda, General Officer Commanding 2 Division.

The projects at Adekunle Fajuyi Cantonment include two 10-person transit accommodation units for corporals and below, five blocks of family quarters for the same ranks, and two houses for regimental sergeants major serving with the 2 Military Intelligence Brigade and 502 Signal Brigade. At Letmauck Cantonment in Mokola, the works include the 81 Battalion Officers’ Mess, sports facilities and semi-detached three-bedroom married officers’ quarters.

Shaibu said personnel should demonstrate discipline, loyalty, integrity, selfless service and professionalism, and maintain high standards of conduct and accountability. He also called on 81 Battalion to preserve its operational effectiveness, work with other security agencies and respond to emerging threats within the division’s area of responsibility. He said the Army was seeking to develop a professional, combat-ready and resilient force amid security challenges across the country.

The Army chief described the new facilities as investments in personnel welfare and operational readiness, saying suitable living conditions could support morale and unit cohesion. He called on beneficiaries to take responsibility for maintaining the buildings and supporting facilities, warning that neglect could undermine their purpose. He also reaffirmed the Army’s commitment to personnel welfare and recognition of troops’ service to national security.

Brigade Commander Uchechukwu Okoroji said the structures had been a welfare concern before renovation and remodelling, and that the improvements could strengthen morale and commitment to duty. 81 Battalion Commanding Officer Lt. Col. Chiemezie Asogwa thanked Shaibu for approving and facilitating the work, describing it as part of efforts to improve conditions for personnel and their families.

title: Pope Leo makes history with US midterm vote
summary: Pope Leo XIV cast a mail-in ballot in Chicago for the US midterms, the first known time a pope has voted in a political election. The Vatican cited civic duty.
body:
Pope Leo XIV has submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago for the US midterm elections, marking the first known time a pope has voted in a political election. The Vatican said Friday that Leo, the first US-born pontiff, voted as a US citizen and supports citizens’ right and duty to take part in democratic processes. The midterms are scheduled for November 3.

The Vatican also confirmed that Leo voted when eligible during his years living in Peru. The pope, born Robert Francis Prevost in Chicago, holds both US and Peruvian citizenship. Before his election as pontiff, he voted in Illinois primary elections, choosing Democratic ballots in 2008 and 2010 and Republican ballots in three later primaries, according to state and local records.

Leo’s vote comes amid a public rift with US President Donald Trump. The two have clashed over the administration’s immigration crackdown and the war on Iran. Trump has criticised the pope’s positions on crime and foreign policy, while Leo has said he is not afraid of the president.

In April, after Trump threatened to destroy Iran, Leo urged people to press political leaders to pursue peace and reject war and violence. In September, he also called on the faithful not to remain passive or indifferent toward current events, urging them to listen, consider the challenges and become involved. His vote is consistent with that public call for civic participation.

title: Nigerian Breweries clears N72.17 billion accumulated losses, moves closer to dividend resumption
summary: Nigerian Breweries reported positive retained earnings at Group and parent-company levels in September 2026. It has not announced a new dividend.
body:
Nigerian Breweries Plc has erased its accumulated losses, reporting positive Group retained earnings of N34.79 billion as of September 30, 2026. That compares with an accumulated deficit of N72.17 billion at the end of December 2025. Retained earnings at the parent company level also turned positive, reaching N37.01 billion from a deficit of N77.09 billion.

The recovery was supported by continued profitability, lower finance costs and stronger cash generation, according to the brewer’s unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30. Nigerian Breweries reported profit after tax of N92.95 billion for the first half of the year, taking Group retained earnings to N13.65 billion by June. A further N21.14 billion in profit after tax in the third quarter brought the nine-month total to N114.10 billion.

Finance costs fell 61.3% to N11.20 billion from N28.90 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. The company also reduced loans and borrowings from N59.71 billion at the end of December 2025 to zero by September 2026. Together, improved profitability and the lower financing burden helped the company absorb its previous accumulated losses and rebuild positive retained earnings at both levels.

The change strengthens the company’s potential capacity to pay dividends, but Nigerian Breweries has not announced a new distribution. Any future dividend would depend on sustained profitability, adequate distributable reserves and the required corporate approvals. The parent company’s retained earnings are particularly relevant because dividend-paying capacity depends on the distributable profits of the legal entity declaring the dividend.

The company has gone three consecutive financial years without a dividend. Its last distribution was for the 2022 financial year, when shareholders received N1.43 per share: an interim dividend of 40 kobo and a final dividend of N1.03. The total payout was approximately N13.87 billion, with the final dividend approved in April 2023. The return to positive retained earnings may raise expectations of a possible distribution for 2026, but no such payment has been confirmed.

title: Stakeholders warn Nigeria’s reliance on imported drug ingredients threatens medicine security
summary: Stakeholders say reliance on imported active ingredients leaves Nigeria exposed to supply disruptions and price swings. They called for targeted local production of essential medicines.
body:
Nigeria’s reliance on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) could leave the country vulnerable to global supply disruptions, trade restrictions and price volatility, stakeholders warned at a meeting in Abuja on Friday. The gathering, organised by Nigeria Health Watch and the World Bank Group, focused on accelerating domestic production of ingredients for priority essential medicines.

Olumide Okunola of the World Bank Group said many Nigerian manufacturers produce finished medicines but depend on imported APIs and other raw materials. The COVID-19 pandemic illustrated how international supply-chain disruptions can affect countries reliant on imported medicines and pharmaceutical inputs. He said Nigeria need not produce every ingredient locally, but should identify essential APIs that can feasibly be made in the country to secure a minimum domestic supply. Inadequate infrastructure, unreliable electricity, limited financing and regulatory bottlenecks remain barriers, he added.

Chris Isokpunwu, permanent secretary of the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, said domestic production could improve supply-chain resilience, reduce exposure to foreign exchange pressures, create skilled jobs and retain more economic value in Nigeria. He cautioned that local production should not come at the expense of quality, efficiency or affordability, and called for a roadmap setting out priority ingredients, investment and infrastructure needs, incentives, regulation and responsible institutions. He also said the African Continental Free Trade Area could open regional markets to Nigerian manufacturers.

Abdu Mukhtar, national coordinator of the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain, said the initiative was working with manufacturers to prioritise APIs based on public health needs. Represented by Zara Abba-Aji, he also described work with the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority on excipient manufacturing and efforts to improve access to finance and technical expertise. The initiative’s MediPool pooled procurement platform is intended to stimulate demand for locally made medicines, he said.

Nigeria Health Watch managing director Vivianne Ihekweazu said the meeting brought government, manufacturers, investors and development partners together to address policy, regulatory and investment barriers. She also raised concern about slow implementation of the federal executive order intended to increase local production of healthcare products. The government has set a target of producing at least 70 per cent of essential healthcare products locally by 2030 and has announced incentives and financing commitments to support domestic manufacturing.

title: INEC omission boosted NDC’s support base, popularity — Gwarzo’s spokesman
summary: Aminu Gwarzo’s spokesman says INEC’s restoration of the Kano candidate’s name has raised NDC support. The party plans to continue voter outreach.
body:
Ibrahim Garba Shuaibu, spokesman for Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Kano State governorship candidate Aminu Gwarzo, says the controversy over the candidate’s name being omitted from an Independent National Electoral Commission list has increased the party’s popularity ahead of the 2027 election. INEC later restored Gwarzo’s name, prompting Shuaibu’s response on Friday.

Shuaibu said the party had not been alarmed by the omission because it believed it had met the electoral requirements. He said NDC members viewed the episode as a temporary setback that would be corrected, pointing to the steps taken from party membership through nomination and submission of the candidate’s details.

He argued that the controversy had generated public sympathy and brought more supporters to the party. Shuaibu said an event that might have been intended as a setback had instead helped strengthen the NDC’s support and encouraged more people to identify with it. These were the spokesman’s claims about the impact of the omission and restoration.

Shuaibu said the party would continue mobilising voters and promoting its programmes across Kano State. He expressed confidence that the episode had improved its prospects in the forthcoming governorship election.

title: Falana urges Nigerians to look beyond Abuja, hold states, LGs accountable
summary: Femi Falana urged Nigerians to scrutinise state and local governments, citing weak accountability and poor services. He called for stronger oversight of council funds.
body:
Human rights lawyer Femi Falana has urged Nigerians to demand accountability from state and local governments, rather than focusing only on the federal government. He made the call in Lagos on Thursday at a screening of *LG Billions in the Dark*, a documentary examining local governance in Osun State. The film highlights a gap between allocations to the state’s 30 local government areas and the condition of roads, water, sanitation, healthcare and education in many communities.

Falana said the problems extend beyond Osun and are connected to weakened local councils and poor accountability. He argued that many residents have lost confidence in local government elections, which he said are often manipulated by ruling parties. He also criticised state authorities for retaining control over council finances despite the Supreme Court’s 11 July 2024 ruling that allocations for Nigeria’s 774 local governments should be paid directly to them from the federation account. Falana said the judgment has not been fully implemented in many states.

He urged residents to use the Freedom of Information Act to ask councils how much money they receive and how it is spent. University of Lagos Vice-Chancellor Folasade Ogunsola said local governments are vital to national development because they are closest to communities. She said councils should have a central role in urban planning and management, support local businesses and improve public spaces and essential services. Ogunsola described direct funding as a step in the right direction, while noting that challenges remain.

Participants in a panel discussion called for councils to publish budgets and spending online in accessible formats and to improve engagement with residents. They also urged greater participation by women, young people and people with disabilities, and recommended digital tools to monitor projects and track public programmes. The event included the unveiling of the Development Reporting Africa Foundation, the non-profit arm of DevReporting, which produced the documentary.

title: Troops Repel ISWAP Attacks In Borno, Kill 48 Terrorists
summary: Troops repelled suspected ISWAP attacks in Yadi and Bitta, Borno State, on October 29, 2026. A military source said 48 fighters were neutralised.
body:
Troops from the Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai, repelled suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) attacks on Yadi and Bitta in Borno State on the night of October 29, 2026, according to a military source. The operations involved air and ground forces.

The source said the attack on Yadi began at about 9 p.m. and continued until 1 a.m. on October 30. A counter-offensive coordinated by the Theatre Command lasted about five hours and used intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance assets alongside air and ground troops.

Forty-eight fighters were neutralised during the operation, the source said, and troops recovered several arms and ammunition. The source also said forces repelled an attack on their camp in Bitta, in Gwoza Local Government Area. Combined air and ground forces defeated the attackers, while troops continued to exploit the area.

title: CAF Reverses Four-Year AFCON Plan, Restores Biennial Tournament
summary: CAF has restored AFCON’s two-year schedule after unanimously reversing its four-year plan. The next editions are set for 2027, 2028, 2031 and 2033.
body:
CAF Reverses Four-Year AFCON Plan, Restores Biennial Tournament

The Confederation of African Football has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations every four years. The CAF Executive Committee unanimously agreed that the tournament would return to a two-year cycle, the governing body said.

CAF President Patrice Motsepe had said at the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026, that the committee would review the four-year plan. The proposed Africa Nations League was expected to replace the biennial AFCON, but CAF concluded it could take several years for the new competition to generate revenue at a level that supports its competitions and football development across the continent.

Motsepe said the decision was intended to protect African football, CAF’s 54 member associations and African players employed by clubs outside the continent. He said the Africa Nations League was expected to deliver financial and development benefits similar to AFCON, but would need time to do so. CAF expects the return to a two-year schedule to provide greater financial benefits for the organisation and its member associations and support the growth of football in Africa.

The next tournament will be held in 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. CAF’s announced schedule also includes editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no AFCON in 2030 because the FIFA World Cup is scheduled for that year; Motsepe said CAF national-team competitions would not be held in the same year as the World Cup, in keeping with FIFA’s tradition.

Motsepe expressed confidence in the three-country hosting arrangement for 2027. He also described AFCON as a platform to celebrate Africa’s diverse cultures and bring together people from the continent’s 54 countries, the African diaspora and the rest of the world.

title: CIBN honours 755 leaders at fellowship investiture
summary: CIBN is set to honour 755 leaders and professionals at its 2026 Fellowship Investiture in Lagos. The programme includes three categories of awards.
body:
The Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) is set to honour 755 leaders and professionals at its 2026 Fellowship Investiture in Lagos tomorrow. The awardees come from banking, government, the private sector and academia. The Institute says the honours recognise contributions to banking, the economy, and the promotion of ethics and professionalism.

The programme will include 18 honorary fellowships, the election of 460 Associates as Fellows, and the induction of 277 senior management staff from banks and academics as Honorary Senior Members. Among those named for recognition are Lagos State Deputy Chief of Staff Sam Egube; Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation Managing Director and Chief Executive Thompson Oludare Sunday; and Bank of Sierra Leone Governor Ibrahim Stevens.

Other awardees include Famfa Oil Limited Vice Chairman Folorunsho Alakija, Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria Managing Director and Chief Executive Olubunmi Kuku, Dangote Cement Plc Chairman Emmanuel Ikazoboh, and Quest Merchant Bank Managing Director and Chief Executive Afolabi Olorode. Ogun State Secretary to the Government Tokunbo Talabi and Summit Bank Limited Managing Director and Chief Executive Siraju Salisu are also listed.

The keynote address, titled “Bank Recapitalisation: Leveraging New Bank Capital for Nigeria’s Industrial Transformation,” will be delivered by Nigerian Economic Summit Group Chief Executive Tayo Aduloju. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite are expected to attend as special guests of honour.

title: Osimhen welcomes second child with partner Stefanie
summary: Victor Osimhen and partner Stefanie Kim Ladewig have welcomed their second child, a daughter named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray announced the birth.
body:
Nigeria and Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen and his partner, Stefanie Kim Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a daughter named Liora Audrey. The Turkish club announced the birth and congratulated the couple, wishing the newborn a long, healthy and happy life.

The announcement came about two weeks after Ladewig, a model, escaped injury in a three-vehicle crash in Istanbul while eight months pregnant. The accident occurred on 13 October in the Mithatpasa neighbourhood of Kemerburgaz, in the city’s Eyupsultan district.

Reports said Ladewig was driving an SUV when it collided with a light commercial vehicle and then veered into another SUV travelling in the opposite direction. The vehicles were damaged, but no injuries were reported. Ladewig was taken to a private hospital in the Maslak area for precautionary checks because of her pregnancy and was later discharged.

Osimhen, 27, is a member of Nigeria’s Super Eagles and plays for Galatasaray in the Turkish Süper Lig. The birth adds to his family life as he continues his professional football career in Türkiye.

title: LASCOPA takes action against Ikeja Electric, resolves 528 consumer complaints
summary: LASCOPA says it resolved 528 of 556 complaints against Ikeja Electric from January to September 2026. Refunds and credit adjustments totalled N26.24 million.
body:
The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency says it resolved 528 of 556 complaints against Ikeja Electric Distribution Company between January and September 2026. The agency’s latest update puts the resolution rate at about 95%, with 28 complaints still ongoing. It also says its interventions secured credit adjustments and refunds totalling N26,243,758.75 for affected consumers.

LASCOPA General Manager and Chief Executive Officer Afolabi Solebo said the agency was committed to fairness, accountability, transparency and improved service delivery in the electricity distribution sector. The agency said its mediation work is intended to help consumers obtain redress and encourage electricity providers to respond to grievances.

Yusuf Musiliu, head of the agency’s Complaints and Mediation Department, said LASCOPA receives and analyses complaints submitted through online and offline channels. Its monthly stakeholders’ parley with Ikeja Electric gives company representatives and affected consumers a regular forum to discuss unresolved cases and seek mutually acceptable agreements. The meetings take place on the last Thursday of each month, according to the agency.

LASCOPA advised consumers to use established complaint procedures rather than resort to self-help. It urged residents raising concerns about estimated bills, excessive charges, overbilling, electricity supply or other service practices to submit supporting evidence, such as bills and payment receipts, to assist investigations and speed up resolution. The agency said its consumer-protection work is carried out under the Lagos State Consumer Protection Law 2025, as amended, and encouraged residents to report grievances promptly.

title: Beyond the battlefield: Crisis communication as a national security imperative, By Mukhtar Ya’u Madobi
summary: A Kaduna symposium urged coordinated crisis messaging to counter deepfakes and disinformation. Participants also called for safeguards for public trust and fundamental rights.
body:
More than 150 representatives of security agencies, emergency services, government, academia and the media gathered in Kaduna for the Second National Symposium on Crisis Communication. Organised by the Centre for Crisis Communication on 27 and 28 October, the event focused on inter-agency cooperation, public trust and cyber threats. Participants argued that coordination between institutions must extend beyond operations to the information they release during emergencies.

Centre chairman Major General Chris Olukolade (rtd) warned that delays or conflicting official accounts can give rumours and manipulated claims room to spread. He cited figures indicating Nigeria had about 109 million internet users at the end of 2025 and estimated cybercrime losses of ₦1.1 trillion between 2017 and 2023. Brigadier General Murtala Abu, representing the Chief of Defence Staff, said cooperation in the field is incomplete without coordinated public communication. He also highlighted the risk that AI-generated audio, images and video could be used to deceive the public.

Participants raised concerns that deepfakes and organised disinformation could affect national security and public confidence, particularly ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kaduna State Commissioner for Information and Culture Ahmed Maiyaki, representing Governor Uba Sani, stressed the role of credible information in building trust. Speakers also recognised that some details may need to be withheld to protect operations, while warning that unexplained silence can fuel speculation.

The symposium’s communiqué proposed an Integrated National Crisis Information Architecture, supported by shared procedures for information exchange and public messaging. It also recommended tools to detect disinformation and deepfakes, improved digital literacy, and regulatory safeguards that protect security while respecting freedom of expression, fundamental rights and due process. The Centre unveiled the Nigerian Journal of Crisis Communication as a platform for research and practical guidance. Participants’ proposals, organisers said, will matter only if institutions put them into practice during future emergencies, sharing verified information promptly and communicating clearly without compromising sensitive operations.

title: ‘X-Men,’ ‘Star Trek’ Star Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
summary: Actor Patrick Stewart, known for “Star Trek” and “X-Men,” has died at 86. He died at home in Los Angeles after a brief journey with two conditions.
body:
Actor Patrick Stewart, best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in “X-Men” films, has died at 86. A statement said he died at his home in Los Angeles, with his wife, Sunny, by his side, after a brief period with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.

Born in Yorkshire in northern England, Stewart began his career on British stages with the Royal Shakespeare Company. He later moved across the Atlantic and built an acclaimed career in American theatre and film.

His performances ranged across genres. A statement described his voice and talent as closely associated with memorable roles, including his work in the Marvel films and as the captain of the Starship Enterprise.

title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations
summary: President Bola Tinubu defended new loans from international institutions and banks amid opposition criticism. He said the investments would expand opportunities for future generations.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, particularly from opposition leaders, over new loans Nigeria has accessed from international institutions and banks.

In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu defended the borrowing plans, saying the investments would expand opportunities for future generations.

The account provided no details about the loans’ amounts, terms or the specific projects they are intended to support.

title: Samson Adamu makes history as CAF confirms Nigerian as General Secretary
summary: Samson Adamu has been confirmed as CAF General Secretary, becoming the first Nigerian to hold the post in the organisation’s 70-year history. The NFF welcomed his appointment.
body:
Samson Adamu has been confirmed as the substantive General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), becoming the first Nigerian to hold the position in the organisation’s 70-year history. The confirmation was announced on Thursday, and the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) congratulated him on his appointment.

Emmanuel Ikpeme, the NFF’s acting general secretary, called the confirmation good news for Nigerian football administration. He said the federation was confident Adamu would succeed and described him as knowledgeable, committed to developing his expertise and experienced across football administration.

Ikpeme said the NFF was pleased with the appointment and would provide the necessary support to Adamu as a member association under CAF. He also wished him success in the role.

Adamu joined CAF, the governing body of African football, as director of competitions and later became director of tournaments and events. On 29 March, he took over as acting general secretary after Veron Mosengo-Omba resigned. His confirmation makes his interim role permanent and gives Nigeria its first holder of the post in CAF’s history.

title: [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
summary: Bola Tinubu arrived in Jeddah on Thursday night for Umrah after departing Abuja earlier that day. He is expected to return to Nigeria next week.
body:
President Bola Tinubu arrived in Saudi Arabia on Thursday night to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage to the Holy City. He landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah after departing Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon.

Tinubu was received at the airport by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi Arabia’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, presidential media aide Bayo Onanuga said the trip would provide an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress. Tinubu is to perform the religious rites associated with Umrah and seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people.

The President is expected to return to Nigeria next week.

title: Police nab masquerades for extorting residents in A’Ibom
summary: Police in Akwa Ibom arrested two Ekpo masquerade participants over alleged extortion and assaults in Ikot Ekpene. Investigators are seeking others linked to the case.
body:
Police in Akwa Ibom State have arrested two Ekpo masquerade participants over allegations of extorting and assaulting residents in Ikot Ekpene. The command said the suspects were detained at about 6 p.m. on Monday, October 26, along the Ukana/Abak highway during an operational show of force. The arrest was announced in a statement released by police spokesperson Timfom John on Thursday.

The suspects were identified as Ine Isong, 29, of Ukana Ikot Esoh Village, and Emmanuel Ekpenyong, 20, of Ikono Local Government Area. Police said they were allegedly found with Ekpo masquerade costumes and attire, as well as machetes, spears and arrows.

According to preliminary reports cited by police, the suspects and other people allegedly involved had been terrorising residents and demanding money from members of the public. The statement also said some people, particularly women, were reportedly assaulted. Police said investigations were continuing to establish what happened and identify others who may be connected to the alleged offences.

Commissioner of Police Baba Azare warned against using cultural practices or masquerade activities to intimidate, extort or harm people. He said the command respected lawful cultural traditions but would act against individuals or groups that took the law into their own hands or threatened residents’ safety.

title: [VIDEO] ‘Four-Year Presidency Is A Gamble,’ Okorocha Faults Obi’s One-Term Promise
summary: Rochas Okorocha called Peter Obi’s proposed four-year presidency a gamble. He urged South-East strategic alliances and backed Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.
body:
Former Imo State governor Rochas Okorocha has criticised Peter Obi’s proposed four-year presidency, calling it a gamble. Obi is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress.

Speaking in a television interview on Thursday, Okorocha said the South-East must learn to be strategic in its alliances. He did not provide further details about what alliances he had in mind.

Okorocha also voiced support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. The former lawmaker representing Imo West said Tinubu had done no wrong to any Igbo man.

title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
summary: Inter and AC Milan unveiled plans for a 71,500-seat stadium to replace San Siro, with construction due to start in 2028. The €1.2 billion venue is planned to open in 2031/32.
body:
Inter and AC Milan have unveiled plans for a shared stadium to replace San Siro, with the new venue expected to open from the 2031/32 season. Named Generali Stadium after its sponsor, the project is scheduled to begin construction in 2028 and is expected to cost the clubs €1.2 billion.

The stadium will hold 71,500 spectators, compared with San Siro’s current capacity of 75,000. Its design, developed by architect Norman Foster and stadium specialist David Manica, is intended to bring fans closer to the pitch. Stands behind the goals will have a steep 37-degree incline, while the overall structure will sit low before rising at either end.

The roof will cover the stands while leaving the pitch exposed. Manica said the design team focused on proximity to the field and acoustics, with the roof intended to amplify crowd noise. He described the project as an effort to carry forward the atmosphere associated with San Siro, rather than simply reproduce its physical form. The venue is also designed to host American football, rugby and concerts.

The clubs paid €197 million to acquire the existing stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they plan to build their new home. San Siro, also known as Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, opened in 1926 and is Italy’s largest stadium. Despite renovations over the decades, the clubs say the venue no longer meets their needs or those of spectators. It is expected to be largely demolished as construction of the new stadium nears completion.

title: APC youth support group urges unity, warns against divisions ahead of 2027 elections
summary: An APC youth support group has backed National Youth Leader Dayo Israel and urged members to resolve disputes through party channels. It called for unity ahead of 2027.
body:
The All Progressives Congress National Young Stakeholders Forum has urged members of the party’s youth wing to respect internal procedures and avoid actions that could deepen divisions ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also expressed support for National Youth Leader Dayo Israel and called on party youths to focus on mobilising for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

At a press conference in Abuja on Thursday, the forum’s National Publicity Secretary, Shehu Attah, said disagreements should be handled by the appropriate party authorities. He cautioned against factional manoeuvres and efforts to establish competing centres of authority, saying such actions could cast doubt on the recognised youth leadership. The forum did not name the people or groups it said were challenging Israel’s office.

The appeal follows public scrutiny of a video Israel posted and later deleted, which showed seven new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado vehicles reportedly allocated to youth leaders for campaign activities. The vehicles prompted questions about resources for political mobilisation. Remi Tinubu had also disclosed that utility vehicles, campaign materials and footwear were being provided for APC youth leaders.

The forum passed a vote of confidence in Israel, describing his office as a link between the party leadership and young members. Attah credited him with initiatives including the APC Youth House, the Nest Resource Centre and Renewed Hope Conversations programmes at tertiary institutions. He also said more than 100 party youths and youth leaders had taken part in overseas training and capacity-building programmes over the past two years.

The group commended Israel’s role in facilitating campaign vehicles for selected youth leaders and the earlier distribution of buses to other party members. Attah said the initiatives had improved morale and addressed calls for greater recognition, while warning that factional disputes could discourage young people seeking a place in the party. The forum urged members to let recognised party structures operate as preparations for the 2027 elections advance.

title: No confusion, Osun will vote Accord candidates, Tinubu for president — Adeleke
summary: Ademola Adeleke says Osun voters should back Bola Tinubu for president in 2027 and Accord candidates for assembly seats. He urged full campaign loyalty.
body:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has said voters should support Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election while choosing Accord Party candidates for the National and State Assembly elections. He said the split in support would not confuse voters, despite the “Rainbow Coalition” effort to mobilise backing for Tinubu’s re-election, led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike.

Adeleke made the remarks on Thursday in Ede while inaugurating a campaign committee for the re-election of Osun West Senator Lere Oyewumi. The governor was represented by his deputy, Kola Adewusi. Adeleke praised Oyewumi, the Senate’s Deputy Minority Leader, and urged committee members to work fully behind his campaign.

Oyewumi credited Adeleke’s leadership and performance with strengthening Accord’s acceptance in Osun. He said the governor’s re-election reflected public support and would help the party’s candidates. Oyewumi also pledged further development in Osun West, including better roads, schools and hospitals, access to clean water and solar streetlights.

Campaign committee Director-General Adesoye Oyetunde praised Oyewumi’s record, saying roads had been tarred in eight of the district’s 10 local government areas, with work launched in the other two. He also cited classroom construction, healthcare support and farm inputs for constituents. Adeleke joined Accord after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party in December 2025. He won re-election on the Accord platform in August, defeating the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, and has also voiced support for Tinubu’s second-term bid.

title: 2027: Makinde visits South-east, speaks on Peter Obi, Igbo’s votes
summary: Seyi Makinde urged South-east voters to look beyond ethnic and religious loyalties in 2027. He outlined his agenda and said his manifesto was due on 4 November 2026.
body:
Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde urged voters in the South-east not to make their choices in the 2027 election on ethnic or religious grounds. Speaking at an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) town hall in Enugu on Thursday, he said the challenges facing Nigeria affected people regardless of their identity.

Makinde, the APM’s presidential candidate, acknowledged that Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate and a former Anambra governor, had strong ties to the region. He said his team had been discouraged from visiting because the South-east was considered Obi’s territory, but that he had come to present his Reset Agenda for Nigeria. He called on voters to reject divisions based on religion or ethnicity.

Makinde said he had held town hall meetings across the country’s six geopolitical zones before releasing his manifesto, arguing that the meetings helped him understand people’s needs. He described the Enugu gathering as the final one and said the manifesto would be prepared over the weekend and launched on 4 November 2026. He outlined four pillars for his agenda: the economy, security, education and socio-political issues. He also promised to govern sincerely, work to rebuild trust between leaders and citizens, and provide an environment in which businesses could thrive. He said youth skills training would support job creation and help reduce unemployment.

At the meeting, South-east campaign coordinator Okechukwu Obiechina said bad leadership had contributed to hardship, including difficulties meeting food, fuel and school-fee costs. APM National Chairman Yusuf Dantalle criticised President Bola Tinubu’s record since his 2023 election and called on him to step aside from the 2027 race. Dantalle also described Makinde, whom he identified as 58, as a candidate representing the youth population. APM vice-presidential candidate Lawal Daura said the party intended to address national challenges through a 16-point agenda and reform the system for the benefit of Nigerians.

title: RCIM share disposal records good progress as investor demand remains robust
summary: RCIM has transferred about 5.2 billion FirstHoldCo shares to investors in a secondary-market disposal. Further transfers await approvals and execution steps.
body:
First HoldCo Plc and RC Investment Management Limited (RCIM) say they have made significant progress in transferring a large block of FirstHoldCo shares held by RCIM as an independent Bridge Holder. The disposal is an orderly transfer of existing shares through the Nigerian Exchange (NGX), rather than a new share issue.

RCIM acquired approximately 10.43 billion FirstHoldCo shares on the NGX in July 2025 under a Central Bank of Nigeria-approved shareholder divestment arrangement. About 5.2 billion shares have since been crossed to subscribers. Further transfers are expected once the required regulatory approvals are secured and the remaining execution processes are completed.

The companies said the large trading volumes in FirstHoldCo shares reflect, to a substantial extent, the transfer of RCIM’s holding to investors. They described subscriptions and the absorption of the sizeable block as evidence of continued investor confidence, citing the group’s financial performance, fundamentals and long-term growth prospects.

The statement also pointed to shareholder returns. On a total shareholder return basis, First HoldCo ranks first among the FUGAZ banking groups, with returns of more than 200% from the beginning of January 2026 to date, it said. The disposal is intended to complete the divestment programme in an orderly manner and broaden FirstHoldCo’s investor base.

title: 2027: Kaduna APC rally won’t erase poverty, insecurity – PRP
summary: The PRP criticised the APC’s Kaduna rally, saying it would not distract from poverty and insecurity. It also called for action over a cleric’s killing.
body:
The Peoples Redemption Party has criticised the All Progressives Congress over its rally in Kaduna, saying campaign events cannot divert attention from poverty and insecurity. In a statement issued in Abuja, PRP National Chairman Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed described the gathering as an expensive effort to project support for the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general elections. He questioned the alleged spending on the event, but the statement did not provide evidence for the amount or establish how it was funded.

Baba-Ahmed said economic hardship and security concerns would remain central to public debate, and argued that political gatherings could not substitute for a record of effective government. He said Nigerians should not interpret the rally as proof that they were satisfied with the APC’s performance. The criticism comes as parties begin positioning themselves ahead of the next general election, when the Tinubu administration’s record is expected to feature in political debate.

The PRP chairman also raised concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s health and called for close medical scrutiny and management. The statement offered no medical evidence to support those concerns. Baba-Ahmed further alleged that attacks and abductions continued during the rally, including abductions from homes in Kaduna metropolis, while police were deployed to protect billboards at the event.

He condemned the killing of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka at his home in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, and called for those responsible to be arrested and prosecuted. Baba-Ahmed said citizens had a right to expect protection regardless of their political views, and urged the government to prioritise security and welfare. He maintained that a credible election in 2027 would end the APC’s leadership, while saying Nigerians would continue to demand safety and dignified living conditions in the meantime.

title: Seplat discovers 157 billion cubic feet of gas, 19 million barrels of oil in Nigeria
