summary: Seplat estimates Aku-01 holds 157 Bcf of gas and 19 million barrels of oil in place. It plans further evaluation and another exploration well in 2027.
body:
Seplat Energy has reported an estimated 157 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 19 million barrels of oil in place at its Aku-01 exploration well in Nigeria. The company disclosed the find on October 29 in unaudited results for the nine months to September 30, 2026. The discovery occurred after the period ended.

The oil was unexpected: Seplat said its original exploration programme anticipated natural gas, but not crude oil. Preliminary assessments indicate substantial hydrocarbon resources, though further work is needed to establish how much can be commercially recovered. Seplat is working to complete the well for potential future production and plans to connect it to existing infrastructure to support early development.

The discovery has lowered exploration uncertainty across four nearby prospects in the licence area, the company said. Seplat plans to drill a second exploration well in the Aku area in 2027. It holds a 40% operated interest in Petroleum Prospecting Licence 2A25, where Aku-01 is located.

For the nine-month period, Seplat’s combined working-interest production averaged 144,999 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 7% from a year earlier. Average crude oil and condensate output rose about 1.4% to 103,173 barrels per day, while natural gas production increased 11.6% to 194.9 million standard cubic feet per day. Natural gas liquids output more than doubled, reaching 8,222 barrels per day.

Revenue rose to N3.78 trillion from N3.36 trillion in the same period of 2025. Pre-tax profit increased 52.75% to N1.34 trillion, compared with N878.99 billion a year earlier. Seplat declared a third-quarter dividend of 19 US cents per share, comprising a 5-cent core dividend and a 14-cent special dividend. That brought dividends declared for the first nine months of 2026 to 40 US cents per share.

title: Ondo govt appoints committee for Fasoranti’s burial
summary: Ondo State named a committee led by Kayode Ajulo to coordinate Reuben Fasoranti’s state burial with his family and Afenifere. His family set Dec. 17 for the funeral.
body:
The Ondo State Government has appointed a committee to coordinate a state burial for Reuben Fasoranti, the late Afenifere leader who died on 20 October at the age of 100. The committee is to work with his family and Afenifere’s leadership to arrange a dignified farewell. The government has not announced a date or detailed programme for the state burial; the family has scheduled the funeral service and interment for 17 December.

Kayode Ajulo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, will chair the committee, with Eniola Olushola as secretary. Its other members are Gbenga Fasua, Gbenga Atiba, Kosemani Kolawole, Bakkita Bello, Idowu Otetubi, Modupe Martins, George Asonja, Muyiwa Ogunyemi, Stephen Abitogun and Adetunji Gbenga.

The committee’s formation was announced in a statement by Ebenezer Adeniyan, the governor’s Chief Press Secretary. The statement said the government approved the state burial in recognition of Fasoranti’s contributions to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria. Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa believes the late elder statesman should be honoured for his years of service, wisdom and selfless leadership, it added.

Fasoranti was an educationist and a prominent figure in progressive politics and the struggle for democracy. His political career was associated with Obafemi Awolowo’s tradition, including the defunct Action Group and later the Unity Party of Nigeria. He served as commissioner for finance in the government of Ondo State Governor Adekunle Ajasin from 1979 to 1983, and later became one of the leading figures in Afenifere.

Separately, on Wednesday, the Senate considered a motion by Adeniyi Adegbonmire, who represents Ondo Central, urging the federal government to name an educational institution after Fasoranti in recognition of his contributions to education and national development.

title: Carrick not surprised he’s still Man Utd manager
summary: Michael Carrick said he was not surprised to remain Manchester United manager and needs no assurances, despite an eight-game winless run. United face Chelsea on Saturday.
body:
Michael Carrick said he was not surprised to remain Manchester United manager despite mounting pressure over the club’s results. Speaking ahead of Saturday’s away match against Chelsea, he said his focus was on improving the team and that he did not need assurances from the club’s leadership about his future.

United have gone eight games without a win. Their 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday left them one point above the Premier League relegation zone. The club have won two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, while seven points from their first eight league games marks their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years.

Carrick’s position has drawn scrutiny during the run of poor results. Bruno Fernandes was left out of the starting line-up against Bournemouth after criticising Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 defeat by Como. Carrick described the decision to bench the United captain as one made for that game and said Fernandes remained committed to the club.

Carrick received applause from supporters as he left the pitch after the Bournemouth match, while players were booed. Former United captain Gary Neville said earlier on Thursday that sometimes a manager needs to be sacked for their own good. Carrick said he would not walk away, adding that he understood the responsibility of the role and cared about what supporters saw from the team. He said the players were hurting over their results but remained hungry to improve.

title: Minister demands results from colleges of education under dual mandate
summary: Education Minister Tunji Alausa urged colleges to show measurable gains under the dual mandate. Eligible colleges can offer the NCE and approved education degrees.
body:
Education Minister Tunji Alausa has urged provosts of colleges of education to demonstrate results under the dual-mandate policy, with stronger accountability and improved teacher preparation. He said the reform could strengthen colleges and widen opportunities for academic and professional advancement, but would require strategic leadership and cooperation among stakeholders.

Alausa’s remarks were delivered by Dr Cecilia Uba, the Federal Ministry of Education’s Director of Colleges of Education, at the National Commission for Colleges of Education Teacher Education Leadership and Impact Award ceremony in Abuja on Thursday. The event, held in partnership with Gosima Group, was part of the commission’s retreat and workshop on implementing the dual mandate and its strategic plan. The policy allows eligible colleges to offer both the Nigeria Certificate in Education and approved bachelor’s degree programmes in education.

The minister reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to working with the NCCE, provosts and other stakeholders to improve the quality and relevance of teacher education. He also said award recipients should treat the recognition as a call to greater responsibility, innovation and service. NCCE Executive Secretary Dr Angela Ajala urged colleges to improve performance, strengthen teacher preparation, support research and adopt digital innovation, while pursuing academic excellence and financial sustainability.

Former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim said teacher education was important to national development and called for modern facilities, sustainable funding and stronger professional development. Gosima Group President and Group Managing Director Dr Gideon Chidiebere Osi said the company planned to expand scholarships for deserving students through its charitable foundation. He said its partnership with the NCCE would support educational leadership and teacher education through scholarships, mentorship and youth leadership development.

title: Police Foil Kidnap Plot In Kano, Arrest Two Suspects
summary: Kano police say they arrested two suspects over a threat to kidnap a village head in Gezawa. Investigations are continuing ahead of a court arraignment.
body:
Police in Kano State say they have foiled an attempted kidnapping in Gezawa Local Government Area and arrested two suspects accused of threatening to abduct the village head of Bangare, Mallam Idris. The suspects were arrested by officers attached to the Gezawa Division during intelligence-led operations.

According to a statement from police spokesperson CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Idris reported the threat on October 26, 2026. He told police he had received a threatening phone call from an unidentified caller on October 24 at about 9:33 p.m.

The command said officers acted after receiving the report and arrested the suspects following sustained follow-up and intelligence-led work. Police said the suspects had confessed to the crime, while investigations continued ahead of their arraignment in court.

Kano State Commissioner of Police CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori commended the officers for their response and reiterated the command’s zero-tolerance stance on criminal activity. He said the operation reflected the Inspector-General of Police’s emphasis on intelligence-led and technology-driven policing, professionalism and proactive crime prevention. The command urged residents to stay vigilant and report suspicious people or movements to the nearest police station.

title: 2027: Abia CP warns politicians against violence, intimidation
summary: Abia police chief Wilfred Afolabi urged parties to avoid violence and notify police before rallies. INEC pledged neutrality and advised candidates to challenge results in court.
body:
Abia State Commissioner of Police Wilfred Afolabi has urged political parties and their supporters to avoid violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and property damage ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also asked parties to notify police in writing before holding rallies, processions and other political activities so security arrangements can be made.

Afolabi spoke at a peace accord signing in Umuahia attended by the Independent National Electoral Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioner, Prof. Sylvia Agu, representatives of security agencies, registered political parties and campaign teams. The accord was read to participants after the police command’s legal officer reviewed relevant electoral laws. Party representatives then signed, pledging to pursue their political ambitions peacefully.

The police commissioner said the command was committed to providing professional and impartial security for all candidates, parties and supporters. He said police had strengthened security through intelligence gathering and analysis, crime mapping, a revamped Cybercrime Unit and improved operational response. Afolabi also acknowledged Governor Alex Otti’s directive on security for campaigns and related activities, and pledged continued cooperation with INEC, security agencies and political stakeholders to protect lives and property.

Agu said INEC would serve all candidates equally and provide a level playing field. She urged candidates to maintain peace before, during and after the election, and to accept the outcome of a free, fair and credible poll. Those dissatisfied with the results, she said, should seek redress through the courts rather than resort to violence or undermine the electoral process. Agu said the accord was intended to prevent conflict by committing signatories to peaceful conduct throughout the election period.

title: Ethiopia receives Russian fighter jets, air defence systems
summary: Ethiopia says it has received 12 Russian Su-35 jets and expects four S-400 systems. The deliveries come amid renewed fighting in Tigray.
body:
Ethiopia has received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets and expects four S-400 air-defence systems, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said. The deliveries are intended to strengthen the country’s military capabilities as fighting intensifies in the northern Tigray region. The S-400 systems are expected but have not been reported as delivered.

Abiy said the aircraft were supplied under an earlier agreement with the Russian government and arrived a year ahead of schedule. He described the delivery as a milestone in efforts to strengthen national security, and said the jets would support Ethiopia’s sovereignty as well as regional security and stability. He also said Ethiopia had become the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to possess this type of advanced combat technology.

The announcement coincided with the start of a two-day Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, which Abiy is attending. The gathering is described as an effort by Russian President Vladimir Putin to expand Russia’s presence in Africa. Abiy has called Putin a close friend of Ethiopia.

The military deliveries come amid renewed clashes between Ethiopian government forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front. TPLF forces had taken control of Mekelle and Alula Aba Nega Airport, but government and allied forces retook Mekelle on Sunday after the group said it had temporarily left the regional capital to operate elsewhere. Eritrean troops crossed into Tigray in early October, adding to tensions and concerns about a wider regional conflict.

title: Argentine football fan jailed for threatening Di Maria over return
summary: A Rosario court sentenced Sergio Di Vanni to 7.5 years for threats aimed at deterring Angel Di Maria’s return to Argentina. Di Maria joined Rosario Central in 2025.
body:
A court in Rosario sentenced football supporter Sergio Di Vanni to seven and a half years in prison on Wednesday for directing threats at Angel Di Maria’s family. The court found the 45-year-old guilty of ordering intimidation intended to dissuade the former Argentina international from returning from abroad to play for Rosario Central, his boyhood club.

The threats took place in March 2024, when Di Maria was playing for Benfica and considering a return to Argentina. They included gunshots fired near a gated community where he owns a property, as well as a pig’s head marked by a bullet wound left outside an estate agency run by his sister. A message threatening his daughter was also reported.

Prosecutors identified 25-year-old Belen Gutierrez as one of the people involved. She was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in June after reaching a plea agreement. A third suspect remains in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors alleged the threats were carried out in exchange for four million pesos, equivalent to $2,600, and linked the campaign to an internal power struggle among supporters of Newell’s Old Boys. Di Vanni’s sentence also covers separate offences connected to his involvement in the supporters’ group.

Rosario Central and Newell’s Old Boys are the city’s two major clubs and fierce rivals. Di Maria initially dropped plans to return to Argentina because of concerns for his family’s safety, but later changed his mind and joined Rosario Central in 2025. He has spent the past two seasons at the club, which won the Argentine title at the end of 2025.

title: Naira holds the N1350/$ baseline despite attractive US yields
summary: The naira settled at N1,349 per dollar as the Fed held rates, keeping US yields attractive and limiting portfolio inflows. Oil receipts and CBN intervention support the currency.
body:
The naira settled at N1,349 per dollar in midweek trading after the US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged and signalled that borrowing costs could remain high. The decision supports the appeal of US assets, with Treasury yields near 5%, and the dollar index trading around 102.25 in early European hours on Thursday.

High US yields have helped constrain foreign portfolio investment into Nigerian bonds and other local assets, limiting one potential source of foreign exchange. At the same time, attractive nominal returns in Nigeria’s bond market may encourage risk-conscious investors to keep their holdings in naira, rather than convert them into dollars. The balance between those forces is one factor shaping the exchange rate.

Oil earnings provide another source of support. Nigerian crude was reported at about $115 a barrel, and higher export revenues could help the Central Bank of Nigeria build gross reserves and strengthen its capacity to manage external shocks. The CBN has also supplied foreign exchange directly to dealer banks to address backlogs and support liquidity in the market.

The exchange rate is expected to move within a N1,340–1,370 per dollar range in the near term, with CBN intervention and oil inflows providing support. Traders are also watching the next CBN Monetary Policy Committee meeting for signs of whether Nigerian rates could be cut, which might narrow the positive real-rate gap with the United States.

In the US, policymakers said they would rely on incoming data when deciding their next steps. Market attention is focused on the September personal consumption expenditures inflation report, due Friday. If inflation rises again and prompts the Fed to resume rate increases, outflows from Nigerian local debt could intensify, adding pressure to the naira.

title: Tinubu To Induct Five Helicopters Acquired By NAF
summary: President Bola Tinubu is expected to induct five new Nigerian Air Force helicopters in Abuja. He is also set to commission the reconstructed hangar housing them.
body:
President Bola Tinubu is expected to induct five helicopters acquired by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) at a ceremony in Abuja. He is also expected to commission the service’s newly reconstructed hangar, where the aircraft are housed.

The helicopters comprise two H-125s manufactured by Airbus Helicopters and three AW-109 Trekker Bs made by Italy’s Leonardo Helicopters. The induction is scheduled to take place at the hangar on the presidential wing of Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport.

The NAF received the aircraft in stages. The two H-125 helicopters had been delivered earlier, while the three AW-109 Trekker Bs arrived in Lagos as part of a separate batch of 10 helicopters acquired by the Federal Government. The other seven aircraft in that batch are expected to be delivered before the end of 2026.

The acquisition is part of the Federal Government’s investment in strengthening the air force’s operational capabilities. It also comes amid broader efforts to modernise and re-equip the Armed Forces to respond to evolving security threats and sustain operations against insecurity.

title: Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu
summary: The APM urged President Bola Tinubu to disclose his destination and stay in Nigeria to address hardship. It also questioned his 2027 electoral prospects.
body:
Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu

The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has called on President Bola Tinubu to disclose his actual destination and remain in Nigeria to address the difficulties facing citizens. The party questioned whether the announced lesser Hajj pilgrimage was the full purpose of his trip, arguing that the country’s problems required attention at home.

In a statement, APM National Publicity Secretary Abubakar Yusuf said the pilgrimage should be devoted to prayer and supplication, not used as a cover for other activities. He accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening hardship and said the President should focus on resolving what he described as burdens placed on ordinary Nigerians.

Yusuf also invoked the expression “Andrew, check out,” urging Tinubu not to leave the country. The party’s appeal tied its criticism of the proposed trip to its broader contention that the President should address domestic challenges rather than depart while citizens face hardship.

Looking ahead to the 2027 presidential election, Yusuf said Tinubu could struggle to win at least 25 per cent of votes in 12 selected states. He expressed confidence that the APM’s presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, would defeat the President, describing Makinde as a hardworking and energetic contender. Yusuf also said Makinde could challenge Tinubu’s political strength in the South-West and elsewhere in the South.

title: Akpabio alleges payment for social media attacks on Tinubu
summary: Senate President Godswill Akpabio urged northern youths to campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election. He alleged some online critics are paid.
body:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio has urged young people in northern Nigeria to build grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 election. He made the appeal on Wednesday during a visit to his office by the Arewa Revival Project, a group with members from the 19 northern states. The group presented Akpabio with an award for his contributions to nation-building.

Akpabio alleged that some people criticising Tinubu and his supporters on social media were being paid, while the young people he addressed were not. He encouraged them to convene youth groups and engage people directly, saying they should challenge what he described as propaganda and explain the case for continuity in government. The allegation was not accompanied by evidence in the account of his remarks.

He defended the administration’s economic policies, including tax reforms, and said the government was seeking to move Nigeria away from reliance on crude oil. Akpabio praised Tinubu’s handling of challenges and said he and members of the National Assembly had given the President a pass mark and endorsed him for a second term. The 2027 election is expected to include Tinubu seeking re-election, with opposition parties aiming to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Akpabio also addressed insecurity and the proposed creation of state police. He said the constitutional amendment process was nearing completion and claimed about 30 state assemblies had endorsed the proposal. He predicted a decentralised policing system could be established within a month, while expressing confidence that the country would overcome its security challenges. Earlier, Arewa Revival Project coordinator Mustafa Ibrahim said the award recognised Akpabio’s national contributions and the National Assembly’s work under his leadership.

title: Katsina APC declares Funtua campaign peaceful amid reports of attacks in Malumfashi
summary: Katsina APC said its Funtua campaign launch was peaceful, while reports described attacks on supporters travelling through Malumfashi. Injury and damage totals remain unclear.
body:
The All Progressives Congress in Katsina State described Wednesday’s Tinubu–Dikko 2027 campaign launch in Funtua as peaceful, saying no clashes, injuries or property losses were recorded at the Funtua Township Stadium. The party’s state chairman, Bishir Saulawa, thanked Governor Dikko Radda, security agencies, party members and other stakeholders for their conduct at the event.

Separate reports described attacks on supporters travelling to Funtua through Malumfashi Local Government Area. Some supporters alleged that groups of youths threw stones and bottles and used other weapons. Those affected reported injuries and lost belongings, while some vehicles had damaged windscreens. Stones were also reported around the Malumfashi town roundabout, near the road linking Bakori Local Government Area.

The reported incidents were along the route to the campaign, not necessarily at the stadium. The APC chairman’s statement did not address the allegations or clarify whether his account covered supporters travelling to the event. The number of people injured, the extent of the damage and who carried out the attacks have not been established.

At the launch, Radda urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu and APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. He identified security, infrastructure, education, healthcare and economic opportunities as priorities, and called on candidates and supporters to campaign peacefully and respect voters’ choices. Deputy Governor Faruk Jobe, former governors Aminu Masari and Ibrahim Shema, lawmakers and other party stakeholders attended. Saulawa presented party flags and banners to candidates for three Senate seats, 15 House of Representatives seats and 34 State Assembly seats.

title: Spain Begins Three-Day Mourning After Latest Train Tragedy Kills 68
summary: Spain began three days of mourning after a train collision killed 68 people and injured scores. Investigators face questions about a reported rail-control failure.
body:
Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after a collision between two high-speed trains in Castilla-La Mancha killed 68 people and injured scores. The crash happened on Wednesday morning on the line connecting Madrid and Seville, when a Renfe train struck the back of a stationary train operated by Iryo. Emergency crews searched the wreckage overnight, using cranes to move twisted metal as they looked for further victims.

Passengers described severe impacts and chaotic scenes inside the Renfe train. One survivor said he woke to find himself thrown into the air; another, who suffered head injuries, said a last-minute seat change may have saved his life. In the nearby village of Urda, a school was opened for relatives seeking information. Red Cross teams provided support, while Civil Guard offices in Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville collected DNA samples to help identify missing people. Blood donation points were also established in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid.

Transport Minister Oscar Puente said an automatic control system had failed along 69 kilometres of track, leading to trains being stopped. He said the control centre then resumed traffic despite circumstances he described as inexplicable. According to Puente, the Renfe train travelled 25 kilometres before hitting the Iryo, and the control centre had time to identify and address the error. The cause of the collision has not been established in the supplied account.

The disaster has renewed scrutiny of rail safety in Spain. In January, a derailment in Andalusia led to two high-speed trains colliding after one crossed onto an adjacent track; 46 people died. That investigation remains ongoing, and the government has faced criticism over its management of the rail network. Families of those killed and missing now face a difficult process of identification and grief, with support workers warning that people will respond to the loss in different ways.

title: 2027: Fubara urges Rivers monarchs to remain neutral
summary: Rivers Governor Siminalayi Fubara urged traditional rulers to promote fairness and peace ahead of the 2027 elections. He also addressed their welfare requests.
body:
Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara has urged traditional rulers to remain fair and promote peace as political activity increases ahead of the 2027 general elections. He made the appeal while opening the 126th, 127th and 128th combined quarterly meeting of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers in Port Harcourt on Wednesday.

Fubara said traditional leaders’ roles in administering justice and ensuring fairness made it important for them to avoid conduct that could divide communities or trigger crises. He asked them to honour the oaths and constitution they accepted before taking their stools, and to put Rivers State’s interests above personal sentiments. He said prioritising the state’s interests was also a principle he applied in governing.

Addressing requests for improved welfare, Fubara said delays in meeting some past requests were due to the council’s inability to organise its own affairs, rather than a failure by the state government. He also said stipends paid to traditional rulers by local government councils were a statutory benefit under the constitution, which a governor could not change through a verbal announcement. Fubara said he would fulfil his promises to the rulers before leaving office next year.

Earlier, council chairman and Paramount Ruler of Apara Kingdom, Chike Amadi Worlu Wodo, thanked the state government for maintaining cordial relations with the traditional institution. He said rulers were well placed to help resolve disputes because of their proximity to communities, including conflicts over chieftaincy, family matters and land ownership.

title: ALTON urges states to scrap telecoms right-of-way fees
summary: ALTON says right-of-way fees can make up 50–60% of fibre costs in some states and wants free access, especially in underserved rural areas. It also seeks targeted incentives.
body:
The Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) has called on state governments to abolish right-of-way charges for telecommunications infrastructure. The association says the fees can account for as much as 60 per cent of fibre-optic deployment costs in some states, making it harder to extend networks to underserved communities. Right-of-way charges are fees for permission to install infrastructure on public or private land and roads.

ALTON Chairman Gbenga Adebayo made the appeal on Tuesday at the 2026 Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja. He said that in some states the charges represent 50 to 60 per cent of the cost of deploying a kilometre of fibre. That expense, he argued, can make projects difficult to justify in places where expected revenue is unlikely to cover construction costs.

Adebayo urged lawmakers to establish free access for telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in rural communities and other areas with limited commercial prospects. He also called for incentives for operators investing where deployment costs exceed likely returns. The Universal Service Provision Fund, which is intended to support areas lacking coverage, could be used more strategically, he said. Adebayo rejected the view that operators were unwilling to invest in rural areas, pointing instead to the economics of building networks there.

He also called for more investment in fibre-optic cables, telecommunications sites and network capacity, saying infrastructure is needed to improve service quality and support emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. At the same summit, Senate ICT and Cybersecurity Committee Chairman Shuaib Salisu said the National Digital Economy and E-Government Bill had reached its third reading and that lawmakers were working on cybersecurity reforms and reviewing the Data Protection Act. He also pointed to the government’s planned 90,000-kilometre fibre network as a way to extend connectivity to underserved communities. Salisu urged businesses to engage lawmakers early so legislation reflects industry conditions and investment needs.

title: CBD COP17: Why African countries struggle to mobilise biodiversity funding – AfDB official
summary: African governments need to embed biodiversity in national investment plans and fund implementation, an AfDB official said at CBD COP17. Fragmented finance and competing priorities remain barriers.
body:
African governments should make biodiversity conservation a central part of national investment priorities and provide resources to carry out commitments, African Development Bank (AfDB) official Arona Soumare said during a discussion on the sidelines of CBD COP17 in Yerevan, Armenia. Soumare, the bank’s Chief Climate Change and Green Growth Officer, said countries often approach development financiers for other priorities, with biodiversity treated as an additional element rather than a main investment objective.

The panel, organised by the World Wide Fund for Nature, examined findings from Africa’s seventh national reports on progress and gaps in delivering the Global Biodiversity Framework. Soumare said governments needed to move beyond commitments under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and show their intent through concrete funding and investment decisions. He said the bank had received many biodiversity project proposals from external organisations, while strong proposals led by African governments were less common.

Soumare described the fragmentation of funding across development sectors as a major obstacle. The AfDB works with countries through Country Strategy Papers, which set out national development priorities and help shape the bank’s investment portfolios. He said biodiversity should be integrated into those priorities alongside areas such as infrastructure, food security and livelihoods, rather than handled separately. Madagascar, he said, offered an example of how country allocations could support private-sector initiatives for national parks and help attract further finance.

He called for financing that could serve both large conservation programmes and smaller community-led projects. While the bank offers funding opportunities to grassroots organisations, available resources do not meet demand: Soumare said a call for proposals might receive enough funding for only three of every 10 applications. He also pointed to blended finance, green banks, green credit lines and nature-related bonds as ways to channel more investment into conservation.

Daniel Mukubi, of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, also identified inadequate financing as a constraint. He said conservation competes with urgent needs including food security, energy, infrastructure and poverty reduction. Regional cooperation, he added, can help build institutional capacity. He cited training for technical experts in geographic information systems and biodiversity mapping, which could support planning for the global goal of conserving at least 30 per cent of land, inland waters and coastal and marine areas by 2030.

title: Solid Minerals: FG Inaugurates Nigeria-US Committee On Strategic Cooperation
summary: Nigeria has inaugurated a committee to advance its minerals partnership with the US. Minister Dele Alake denied claims that Nigeria sold $700 billion in minerals.
body:
The Federal Government has inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja, weeks after the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding on developing Nigeria’s mining industry. The committee is intended to advance the partnership and identify ways to turn the agreement into practical outcomes.

Solid Minerals Development Minister Dele Alake rejected claims that Nigeria had sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States. He said Nigeria had not sold its mineral assets and described the agreement as a government-to-government framework intended to connect American investors with Nigerian businesses.

The memorandum was signed in September on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Alake signed for Nigeria with US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau at the Nigerian Mission House in New York. The stated areas of cooperation include attracting investment, sharing technology, expanding local processing and creating jobs.

Alake said the government wants mineral resources to generate more value within Nigeria and contribute to the country’s effort to reduce its dependence on oil. Local processing, he said, is now a key requirement for investors seeking mineral titles. He also said the partnership could bring together Nigeria’s resources with US capital and technology to support the mining sector.

The minister called on the committee to work diligently, identify viable investment opportunities and produce measurable results in support of President Bola Tinubu’s $1 trillion economy target. At the signing, Alake said implementation of the agreement would support the administration’s economic diversification agenda and promote industrial growth. Landau was quoted as supporting a US partnership with Nigeria.

title: AU accredits Nigeria’s counter-terrorism centre for West Africa
summary: The AU accredited Nigeria’s counter-terrorism centre as a regional hub for West Africa and the Sahel. Its renewable three-year mandate includes training and threat analysis.
body:
The African Union has accredited Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) as an African Union Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism for West Africa and the Sahel. The designation expands the centre’s role in supporting AU member states through specialised training, joint threat analysis, research, technical assistance and exchanges of lessons learned.

The accreditation was announced on October 27, 2026, at the conclusion of the African Lessons Learned Forum in Abuja. The Acting Director of the African Union Counter Terrorism Centre, Dr Idriss Mounir Lallali, said the recognition followed an assessment of the NCTC’s governance, institutional capacity, training programmes, analytical capabilities, coordination mechanisms and adherence to human rights and the rule of law. The accreditation will initially run for three years and may be renewed.

The process began with a memorandum of understanding between the AU and the NCTC in September 2025. A technical assessment mission in Abuja in December that year produced a roadmap setting out the institutional requirements for accreditation. The NCTC subsequently strengthened its governance structures, training curricula, operational procedures, analytical and coordination functions, and human-rights safeguards.

The centre operates under Nigeria’s Office of the National Security Adviser. Its regional role reflects President Bola Tinubu’s vision, announced at a high-level African counter-terrorism meeting in Abuja in April 2024, to develop the NCTC as a hub for intelligence sharing, operational coordination, training and capacity building.

National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, represented at the event by NCTC National Coordinator Major General Adamu Garba Laka, described the accreditation as both recognition of Nigeria’s progress and a responsibility to contribute further to collective African security. Ribadu said the Federal Government and the Office of the National Security Adviser would support the expanded mandate through staffing, sustainable resources and institutional partnerships, while maintaining compliance with accreditation standards.

title: FEC approves ₦631.3 billion for nine road projects nationwide
summary: FEC approved about ₦631.3 billion for nine road projects nationwide. Works Minister David Umahi also outlined progress on major corridors and regional highway plans.
body:
The Federal Executive Council has approved approximately ₦631.3 billion for nine road projects across Nigeria. Works Minister David Umahi announced the decisions after Wednesday’s council meeting, chaired by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the State House in Abuja. He said the projects are intended to improve transport links, connectivity and economic activity through road construction, reconstruction and rehabilitation.

Among the approvals, ₦167 billion was allocated to reconstruct the 95-kilometre Etuke–Okeni–Ankpa–Otopa Road in Kogi State. The council also approved ₦209 billion for the 81.1-kilometre Ado–Ilawe–Ilumaba–Ikole Road in Ekiti, including a bridge, and ₦62 billion for the Tungo–Karamti Road between Adamawa and Taraba, which will include five bridges. Other allocations include ₦20.257 billion for an 18-kilometre road linking Asiago to the Port Harcourt–Enugu Expressway, and ₦30 billion for remedial work on deteriorated sections of the East–West Road.

Umahi said ₦11.33 billion was approved for a road project previously undertaken by the Abia Government. The funding decision followed the end of the project’s arrangement under the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Ltd. tax-credit scheme. The council also approved ₦28.218 billion to rehabilitate a 17-kilometre section of the Sokoto–Illela Road, Route A1.

The minister reported that the first 118-kilometre section of the Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria Road had been completed in 30 months, including 81 kilometres built with reinforced concrete pavement. Work on the second, 164-kilometre section was nearing completion, with 16 kilometres remaining. He said the full 375-kilometre Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano corridor would have solar-powered streetlights.

Umahi also said ministers from countries along the Lagos–Abidjan coastal highway were due to meet on Friday to discuss financing. The proposed arrangement would involve the African Development Bank lending to participating countries for their sections. The route includes stretches in Nigeria, Togo, Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire and Benin Republic, and is intended to strengthen regional connectivity and trade.

title: Troops Foil Ambush By Terrorists In Zamfara, Recover 520 Livestock In Sokoto
summary: Troops said they repelled an ambush on Zamfara’s Anka–Guruzu Road and rescued two herders. In Sokoto, they recovered 520 livestock after foiling a rustling attempt.
body:
Troops of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, said they foiled a terrorist ambush on the Anka–Guruzu Road in Zamfara State and rescued two abducted herders during a separate operation in Sokoto State. The operations also resulted in the recovery of 520 livestock, according to a military statement issued by task force media information officer Captain Tamuno Sinivie.

The statement said Sector 2 troops came under a coordinated attack on October 28, 2026, while conducting a fighting patrol along the Anka–Guruzu Road. The patrol followed reports of terrorist activity in the area, and attackers were positioned on both sides of the route. Troops returned fire, inflicting what the military described as heavy casualties before the attackers fled. The soldiers then secured the road and restored movement for commuters.

One soldier was shot during the Zamfara encounter and evacuated for medical care. The statement said he was in stable condition. In Sokoto, troops acted on intelligence about an attempt to rustle livestock and abduct herders at Takasaba Village in Sabon Birni Local Government Area. They engaged the suspected attackers, who fled and left behind 520 livestock and two abducted herders, aged 50 and 14. The rescued herders were handed over to Sabon Birni local government authorities.

Operation Fansan Yamma Theatre Commander Major General W. B. Idris commended the troops and urged them to maintain pressure on terrorist groups. He also reaffirmed the military’s commitment to restoring peace and security in the North-West and called on residents to provide security agencies with timely, credible information.

title: Serie A: Inter down Venezia 2-0 as Bologna sink Milan
summary: Inter moved level with Lazio at the top after a 2-0 win over Venezia. Bologna beat Milan 4-2 as Samuel Mbangula scored a hat-trick.
body:
Inter Milan returned to the top of Serie A with a 2-0 win away to bottom-placed Venezia, while Bologna handed AC Milan their first league defeat of the season, winning 4-2 at San Siro. Inter moved level with Lazio on 25 points, ahead of a derby against Milan on Saturday. Milan are fifth on 18 points; Bologna climbed to 11th with 11 points.

Inter’s goals came from Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal, who each diverted a dangerous delivery into their own net in the space of two minutes. The result was less comfortable than the scoreline suggested. Venezia threatened repeatedly, but Lion Lauberbach’s first-half goal was ruled out for offside and goalkeeper Ivan Provedel pushed another of his efforts onto the crossbar. Akor Adams also had a goal disallowed for offside after rounding Provedel.

Inter coach Cristian Chivu said his side needed to recover physically and mentally before the derby, after making several changes at half-time. The team had come into the match following a late comeback win over Fiorentina, their fifth comeback victory of the season. Venezia, who have collected three points all season, remain at the bottom of the standings.

At San Siro, Samuel Mbangula scored three times on his full debut for Bologna. He opened the scoring inside eight minutes, but Milan levelled through Alphadjo Cisse after an error by Arthur Theate. Cisse put Milan ahead in the 27th minute, volleying in a cross from Fikayo Tomori. Bologna then turned the match around: Davide Bartesaghi put a free-kick into his own net, before Mbangula restored the visitors’ lead with a composed finish. He completed his hat-trick late in the game after Bologna won the ball in midfield.

Milan coach Ruben Amorim pointed to fatigue and injuries, saying his depleted side had lacked energy. Elsewhere, Parma and Udinese drew 0-0 after Adrian Bernabé had a penalty saved by Maduka Okoye.

title: 2027: Kwankwaso warns INEC over alleged AI-generated images in voter register
summary: Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso urged INEC to investigate alleged AI-generated images and questionable voter-register entries ahead of 2027. He called for an independent audit.
body:
Former Kano State governor and senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to investigate reports of suspected AI-generated photographs and other questionable records in the preliminary voter register. He raised the issue in a statement posted on his official Facebook page, warning that unresolved concerns could damage confidence in the electoral system before the 2027 general elections.

Kwankwaso questioned how the photographs entered the register, whether the people shown had been registered and whether their identities were properly verified. He said the allegations raised concerns about the integrity of voter registration and the safeguards INEC uses to prevent manipulation. He called on the commission to provide clear answers to the public.

While welcoming INEC’s decision to investigate, Kwankwaso said assurances alone would not be enough. He called for a thorough, transparent and independent inquiry, with its findings made public and anyone found responsible held accountable under the law.

He also urged a comprehensive independent audit of the preliminary register to identify questionable entries, duplicate registrations and possible artificial identities. Kwankwaso said the review must protect eligible Nigerians’ right to vote and should not exclude legitimate voters.

He warned that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, could be used to undermine the electoral process if safeguards were inadequate. In his view, the credibility of the 2027 elections will depend substantially on an accurate and trustworthy voter register.

title: Oluremi Tinubu, NITDA and Nigeria’s digital future, By Shuaib S Agaka
summary: A $10.4 million startup hub is planned for Abuja, alongside ICT centres and digital-skills programmes backed by Oluremi Tinubu and NITDA. Its impact will depend on delivery.
body:
A $10.4 million Renewed Hope Startup Hub is planned for Wuye, Abuja, as part of a broader set of technology and digital-inclusion initiatives involving First Lady Oluremi Tinubu and the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA). The project is funded through a Japanese government grant facilitated by the Japan International Cooperation Agency. NITDA is expected to oversee the hub when it is completed. Plans include hardware prototyping facilities, incubation, mentorship and international partnerships.

The hub adds to community ICT centres established through a partnership between Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Initiative and NITDA. Centres have been inaugurated in Bauchi, Ilorin, Ibadan and Ihugh in Benue State. In January 2025, the Ilorin centre was accompanied by an announced ₦50 million grant for women entrepreneurs. In October 2025, ten digital learning centres were inaugurated virtually across Abia, Delta, Edo, Kano, Katsina, Lagos, Nasarawa, Ondo, Yobe and Zamfara states.

The collaboration also includes technology facilities in higher education. ICT Experience Centres are being developed across the country’s six geopolitical zones with the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, at an estimated cost of about ₦1 billion each. The account says centres have been established at Ekiti State University, the University of Cross River State, Federal Polytechnic Oko and Kwara State University. They are intended to support learning in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics and software development.

Digital-skills programmes form another part of the effort. A Women ICT Training and Empowerment Programme run with NITDA expanded from the Federal Capital Territory to all 36 states and the FCT; more than 600 women had benefited by November 2025. Tinubu’s partnership with Huawei has also supported training for women entrepreneurs in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, 5G and digital transformation. The initiatives aim to widen access to technology and help participants use it productively.

The projects’ longer-term value will depend on whether facilities remain operational, training translates into practical skills, and innovators and entrepreneurs can turn those opportunities into sustainable outcomes. The startup hub is still at the foundation-laying stage, and its planned facilities and oversight arrangements have yet to be tested in operation.

title: Chelsea Win As Bayern, Madrid Share Points In Women’s Champions League
summary: Chelsea beat Roma 2-0 for their second win in the competition. Bayern recovered from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Real Madrid.
body:
Chelsea secured a 2-0 win over Roma in the Women’s Champions League on Wednesday, while Bayern Munich fought back from a two-goal deficit to draw 2-2 with Real Madrid. The result gave Chelsea a second win in this season’s competition after they began with a victory and a draw, scoring once across their first two matches.

Chelsea dominated the first half at Plough Lane but could not find a breakthrough. Alyssa Thompson struck the crossbar, and Aggie Beever-Jones was denied by a last-ditch challenge after a pass from Hannah Hampton. The deadlock ended in the 51st minute: Wieke Kaptein cut the ball back for substitute Ellie Carpenter, who slid her finish under goalkeeper Rachele Baldi. Carpenter was making her 50th Champions League appearance. After Melvine Malard missed a chance to extend the lead, Kadeisha Buchanan headed in Kaptein’s cross in the final minute.

In Munich, Real took the lead through Athenea in the seventh minute, then doubled it 15 minutes later when former Bayern forward Lineth Beerensteyn headed home. Bayern responded soon after, with Edna Imade converting Klara Buhl’s corner. Momoko Tanikawa completed the comeback in the 52nd minute, curling in after Real goalkeeper Merle Frohms had parried a shot from Linda Dallmann.

Before kick-off in Munich, players and supporters observed a moment of silence following a train crash near Madrid earlier on Wednesday that killed at least 68 people. Real’s players wore black armbands. Elsewhere, Servette beat OH Leuven 5-1, with Paola Hernandez and Gloria Marinelli each scoring twice. Arsenal were due to host Benfica in Wednesday’s late matches, while Lyon were set to face Inter Milan.

title: State police: Bauchi Assembly approves constitutional amendment
summary: Bauchi’s Assembly approved recommendations for a constitutional amendment to enable state police. The proposal would let states create services alongside federal policing.
body:
The Bauchi State House of Assembly has approved recommendations on a proposed amendment to the 1999 Constitution that would provide for state police. The resolution was presented during plenary on Wednesday by Deputy Speaker Jamilu Ummaru, who is interim chairman of the House Committee on Constitutional Amendment.

Ummaru said the proposal is intended to strengthen Nigeria’s security arrangements and provide additional support in addressing the country’s security challenges. It would create a constitutional framework allowing state governments to establish their own police services alongside the existing federal security structure.

The Assembly’s approval records the state legislature’s position on the proposed amendment and forms part of the constitutionally prescribed process for changing the 1999 Constitution. The proposal had been transmitted to the state legislature for consideration and approval under the rules governing constitutional amendments.

The resolution does not itself establish state police. It represents the Assembly’s approval of recommendations on the proposed constitutional change.

title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africans deserve better protection’ — Tech experts faults companies, govt over digital safety
summary: TechHerNG’s Chioma Agwuegbo urged platforms and African governments to strengthen digital safeguards. Speakers also stressed child privacy, trust and responsible design.
body:
Technology companies should build user safety, privacy and rights into digital products, TechHerNG executive director Chioma Agwuegbo said at Moonshot 2026: Courage & Conviction. Speaking at a session on safer digital futures at the event’s Startup Stage, she warned that new tools developed without adequate safeguards could expose women, children and people with disabilities to harm. “Access and safety should be the floor,” she said.

Agwuegbo pointed to the use of artificial intelligence to create non-consensual intimate images of women as an example of emerging risks. “For instance, Grok should never be able to nudify women,” she said, urging platforms to consider potential abuse before launching products. She also said African users often have fewer options for redress over online violence than people in some other jurisdictions, and argued that companies were not investing enough in user safety.

She called on African governments and regulators to do more to address digital safety and hold technology companies to appropriate safeguards. On children’s online experiences, Agwuegbo said parents should foster trust and open communication rather than rely only on restrictions. She also urged media organisations to report violence against women responsibly and bring attention to risks in digital spaces.

Modupe Adebimpe, head of operations and projects at ProsperityTech, said embedding safety measures in products can be expensive, but privacy and safety should remain central to development, especially when children are involved. She also emphasised that children have privacy rights, requiring stakeholders to balance protection with respect for personal boundaries. “Trust is a currency, it helps you to retain customers,” she said, highlighting the role of responsible design in maintaining user confidence.

title: 2027: Obi Pledges To Jail Electoral Offenders
summary: Peter Obi says he would tighten electoral laws and prosecute those who manipulate results if elected. He also proposed stricter education requirements for candidates.
body:
Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, has pledged to strengthen electoral laws and impose tougher penalties on those who manipulate elections if elected president. He made the commitment at an NDC town hall meeting in Akwanga Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, where he set out proposed changes to the electoral system.

Obi said his administration would focus on strengthening political parties and improving electoral processes, with the aim of limiting manipulation and rebuilding public confidence in elections. He said electoral fraud should lead to prosecution and imprisonment for Independent National Electoral Commission officials and others found responsible for altering results.

He also proposed stricter educational requirements for people seeking elective office. Aspirants, he said, should be able to demonstrate that they attended primary and secondary school. People who forge academic certificates or falsely claim to have the required educational background should face legal consequences, he added.

Obi said the law should apply equally to citizens and public officeholders, regardless of their status. He described his political ambition as an effort to build a country with functioning institutions, respect for electoral rules and no one above the law. The proposals would require legal and institutional measures to put them into effect, while any changes to candidate eligibility rules would need to comply with Nigeria’s constitutional and electoral framework.

title: 2027: I’ll deal with those who rig elections if… — Peter Obi
summary: Peter Obi says electoral riggers and complicit election officials would face jail under his government if he wins in 2027. He also proposes stricter education rules for candidates.
body:
Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, has vowed that electoral offenders would face jail if he wins the 2027 presidential election. Speaking at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, he told party supporters that election manipulation would not be allowed to go unchallenged in the next general election.

Obi said his administration would strengthen political parties and the electoral process to prevent rigging. He also warned that Independent National Electoral Commission officials and others involved in election administration would be prosecuted if found guilty of manipulating elections under his watch. He said the rule of law should apply to everyone, from the country’s highest officeholder to the last person, and that nobody should be above it.

The former Anambra State governor also called for stricter eligibility rules for election candidates. He said aspirants should be required to have attended both primary and secondary school, and argued that those who had not attended either level or who forged certificates should face jail.

Obi said his political ambition was driven by a desire to change Nigeria and establish a system in which electoral rules are respected. He described strengthening the parties and the electoral process as central to preventing future manipulation.

title: The 2026 french week celebration: showcasing the dynamic economic and commercial partnership between france and nigeria.
summary: France-Nigeria trade reached $4.7 billion in 2025, with firms expanding across sectors. French Week 2026 is scheduled in Lagos from Oct. 30 to Nov. 6.
body:
## French Week 2026 to spotlight France-Nigeria commercial ties

France and Nigeria are seeking to turn expanding economic relations into new business partnerships, with French Week 2026 set to take place in Lagos from October 30 to November 6. Franco-Nigerian Chamber of Commerce and Industry President Guillaume Niarfeix said the week-long program would focus on converting dialogue between businesses into concrete cooperation. The event is described as Nigeria’s largest C-level business networking gathering.

Bilateral trade reached $4.7 billion in 2025, and French foreign direct investment stock in Nigeria stood at €8.1 billion. More than 100 French companies operate in Nigeria across sectors including energy, agriculture, pharmaceuticals, insurance, logistics, infrastructure and hospitality, generating more than 14,000 direct local jobs. Companies named as continuing to invest and expand include TotalEnergies, CMA-CGM, SPIE, Schneider Electric and Danone. Carrefour, Accor and Canal+ have also been expanding their commercial presence, with Canal+ pursuing an acquisition strategy involving MultiChoice.

Infrastructure and energy projects feature prominently in the business ties. Niarfeix cited TotalEnergies’ 2024 final investment decision with NNPC on the Ubeta gas field, intended to supply Nigeria LNG Train 7, as well as the IMA project. The Omi Eko water-transport project, supported by France through AFD alongside the European Union and European Investment Bank, is planned to provide 75 electric ferries, upgrade 25 terminals and serve 15 routes across 140 kilometres of Lagos waterways. At Lekki Deep Sea Port, CMA-CGM has agreed to operate the container terminal, which has a stated annual capacity of 2.5 million TEUs. Agreements advanced in Paris in September 2026 also included partnerships for the Gateway Deep Sea Port and Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone.

Cooperation is also growing in agriculture and technology. The recently formed Franco-Nigerian Agri-Business Club aims to support investment in local capacity, mechanisation, processing and efforts to reduce post-harvest losses. Nigerian firms and institutions are also building links in France: Access Bank opened a French Desk in Paris, while JR Farms and Babafood have established operations there. The Franco-Nigerian Chamber, founded in 1985, has extended its work beyond Lagos through a Paris leadership training program and business mission. Alongside the Chamber, Team France institutions support cooperation in trade, investment, education, culture, innovation and sustainable development.

title: Dockworkers threaten nationwide Port shutdown
summary: Nigerian dockworkers have threatened a nationwide port shutdown next week unless terminal operators begin talks on a revised NJIC agreement. The previous deal expired in May 2026.
body:
Dockworkers in Nigeria have threatened to shut down ports nationwide next week unless terminal operators begin negotiations on a new National Joint Industrial Council (NJIC) agreement. The Dockworkers Branch of the Maritime Workers’ Union of Nigeria (MWUN) said workers were increasingly frustrated by the delay and warned that port operations could be disrupted if talks did not start urgently.

Speaking in Lagos on Wednesday, branch president Bolaji Agboola said the previous NJIC agreement expired at the end of May 2026. Revised rates were expected to take effect from June 1, he said, adding that workers should already be receiving the updated rates.

Agboola said branch leaders were finding it increasingly difficult to contain workers’ agitation. He said they had continued engaging with dockworkers in an effort to prevent the dispute from escalating, but that frustration was growing as negotiations remained stalled.

The union branch called on the Federal Government to intervene through the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA). Agboola urged the agency to ensure that terminal operators began negotiations before the close of work this week. He warned that port operations across the country could be disrupted next week if the dispute remained unresolved.

The dispute concerns a review of workers’ rates under the NJIC agreement. Agboola accused operators of terminals and jetties covered by the agreement of delaying discussions and urged them to begin negotiations without further delay.

title: Reps move to establish College of Nursing in Lagos
summary: The House of Representatives has advanced a bill to establish a federal nursing and midwifery college in Lagos. It aims to expand professional training.
body:
The House of Representatives has passed a bill through its second reading to establish a Federal College of Nursing and Midwifery in Ifako/Ijaiye Local Government Area of Lagos State. The bill, sponsored by Benjamin Olabinjo, who represents the constituency, was presented to the House on Wednesday. It proposes a centre for training, research and continuing education in nursing, midwifery and related fields.

Olabinjo said the college could help increase the number of qualified nurses and midwives available to healthcare facilities. He pointed to staffing shortages and the migration of trained professionals abroad as pressures on Nigeria’s health system. He also argued that Lagos needs more training places, noting that limited federally accredited capacity makes it difficult for some applicants to gain admission.

Under the proposed legislation, the college could award professional certificates, diplomas, degrees and post-basic qualifications. It would be empowered to admit students, conduct examinations and research, organise academic programmes and provide continuing education. Its proposed structure includes a governing council, a School of Nursing, a School of Midwifery and principal officers to oversee administration and academic work.

The bill’s sponsor said expanding training could support patient care and maternal and child health, including by increasing the availability of skilled midwives. He also said the college could create study and employment opportunities in Ifako/Ijaiye and elsewhere in Lagos, and generate activity for local businesses. Olabinjo urged members to support the bill and refer it to the relevant committee for further consideration. The proposed institution would require further legislative approval and presidential assent before it could be established under the law.

title: APC chair attacks Atiku over lack of projects in Plateau as VP
summary: APC chair Nentawe Yilwatda challenged Atiku Abubakar to identify a major Plateau project from his vice-presidential years. He praised Tinubu’s record.
body:
All Progressives Congress National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda challenged former vice-president Atiku Abubakar to identify a major project worth at least N10 billion that was completed in Plateau State during Abubakar’s eight years in office. Yilwatda made the remarks on Wednesday at the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Jos, where he was seeking support for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election.

Yilwatda said he could not recall a major road or other large-scale project delivered in Plateau during that period. He contrasted that record, as he described it, with what he said Tinubu’s administration was bringing to the state. He cited a university and the Federal Medical Centre among the projects associated with the current administration, and said it had addressed issues in healthcare, education, infrastructure and security.

The APC chair identified insecurity as the main concern for Plateau residents and credited Tinubu with addressing it. His comments were made while campaigning for the president’s re-election; the source material did not provide further detail about the projects he named or his assessment of security in the state.

Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang also urged residents to support Tinubu’s re-election. He argued that the president should be allowed to complete an eight-year term, referring to a North-South power-sharing arrangement. Mutfwang said former president Muhammadu Buhari had served eight years representing the North and that the South should likewise be allowed eight years. He also asked Nigerians to be patient with Tinubu’s economic policies, saying they needed time to produce results.

title: Reps Call For INEC Briefing On 2027 Election Readiness
summary: The House has asked INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan to brief its Electoral Matters Committee within seven legislative days. The briefing will cover preparations for the 2027 elections.
body:
The House of Representatives has resolved that Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman Joash Amupitan brief the House Committee on Electoral Matters within the next seven legislative days. The briefing is to address the Commission’s readiness for the 2027 General Elections and its broader preparations for national elections.

Amupitan is expected to update the committee on Continuous Voter Registration and the management of permanent voter cards. Other subjects include election logistics, technology deployment, personnel training, electoral security, risk assessment strategies and budget implementation.

The resolution followed a motion sponsored by the House minority whip and deputy minority leader. The motion initially called for the INEC chairman to brief the full House. The deputy speaker said the Commission had already discussed its preparations publicly at several fora and proposed that the briefing instead take place at committee level. The House adopted that approach.

INEC has also revised the timetable for the general election. It had previously set 20 February 2027 for the Presidential and National Assembly Elections and 6 March 2027 for the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections. The Commission said it adjusted the schedule after the Electoral Act, 2022 was repealed and the Electoral Act, 2026 enacted, changing statutory timelines for pre-election and electoral activities. Under the revised timetable, the presidential and National Assembly polls will take place on 16 January 2027, followed by the governorship and state assembly elections on 6 February 2027.

title: Madrid apologise to Chinese people over Mbappé’s comments
summary: Real Madrid apologised to Chinese people after remarks by Kylian Mbappé reportedly caused offence. The club reaffirmed respect for China and its supporters.
body:
Real Madrid has apologised to the Chinese people over recent remarks by forward Kylian Mbappé that reportedly caused offence. In a statement posted on its X account on Wednesday, the club said it regretted any offence caused and shared an apology Mbappé had already issued.

The club said it respected China, its history, culture and people, and acknowledged the millions of Chinese supporters who follow Real Madrid. Mbappé reportedly expressed regret over his comments and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people.

Real Madrid also said it remained committed to respect, peaceful coexistence and understanding between cultures. It expressed a desire to strengthen its relationship with China and continue the longstanding bonds of friendship with its supporters there. The source material does not provide details of the remarks that prompted the apologies.

title: UK raises student visa proof of funds to £14,130 from November 30
summary: From November 30, 2026, students applying to study in London must show £14,130 for living costs, up from £1,529 per month. The change affects Nigerian applicants.
body:
International students applying for UK study visas will face a higher financial requirement from November 30, 2026. Those studying in London will need to show they can access at least £1,570 per month for living expenses, compared with the current £1,529. The revised requirement amounts to £14,130 for the period covered by the visa maintenance calculation.

The funds are required in addition to tuition fees and other visa-related costs. The change applies to prospective international students, including Nigerians planning to study at British universities, who will need to make additional financial provision before submitting applications. The supplied requirements give a London figure but do not specify a revised monthly amount for students studying elsewhere in the UK.

The increase comes amid rising living costs and financial pressures for international students. Accommodation expenses, limited job opportunities and restrictions on working hours can make it harder for students to meet costs while studying. International students also contribute to the UK’s higher education sector and wider economy.

The new threshold follows earlier changes to maintenance requirements. In January 2025, the monthly amount was raised to £1,483 for London and £1,136 for locations outside the capital. The latest adjustment further increases the funds that students planning to study in London must demonstrate.

title: PDP Chairmen Allege Escalating Political Violence, Opposition Intimidation In Ebonyi
summary: PDP state chairmen called for investigations into alleged violence and restrictions on opposition activity in Ebonyi. Police said the command remains politically neutral.
body:
The Forum of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) State Chairmen has called for investigations into alleged political violence and intimidation of opposition members in Ebonyi State. In a statement issued by its chairman, Imo State PDP chairman Austin Nwachukwu, the forum cited reported threats, abductions, killings, unlawful detentions and property destruction. It said the incidents and restrictions on PDP activity spanned mid-2026 and urged authorities to act ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The forum asked the Inspector-General of Police to establish an impartial panel to investigate reported attacks, threats, abductions, killings, armed robbery and property damage. It also called on the Department of State Services to conduct a comprehensive security assessment and urged President Bola Tinubu to ensure impartial security measures and equal protection for citizens regardless of political affiliation. The group asked Governor Francis Nwifuru, the police, the DSS and the Office of the National Security Adviser to intervene.

The chairmen also called on the United Nations, African Union, ECOWAS, diplomatic missions and international human rights organisations to monitor human rights and democratic freedoms in the state. They said PDP gatherings had allegedly faced bans and restrictions while rival political groups were allowed to use public spaces. The forum described the police response to opposition complaints as unsatisfactory and raised ethical concerns about reported accommodation arrangements between the state Commissioner of Police and ReMeritona Hotel in Abakaliki, which it said is allegedly owned by the governor. It said the arrangement did not establish bias but called for clarification to protect confidence in police neutrality.

The forum urged Nwifuru to reject political violence, clarify reported statements against the opposition, explain the legal basis for sealing party assets and cooperate with independent investigators. It said anyone found responsible for wrongdoing on credible evidence should face the law, regardless of political status. The statement also encouraged PDP governorship candidate Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii and his supporters to remain peaceful as they prepare for the 2027 elections.

In response, Ebonyi State Police Command rejected claims of political bias or compromise. Police spokesperson SP Joshua Ukandu said that, under Commissioner of Police Hope Okafor, the command remained politically neutral and responded promptly and professionally to security threats.

title: Police arrest fake lawyer after 11 years of practice in Ebonyi
summary: Police in Ebonyi arrested Ugwumba Enyinnaya over allegations he posed as a lawyer for more than 11 years. He has been charged to court.
body:
Police in Ebonyi State have arrested Ugwumba Enyinnaya, who they allege posed as a lawyer and practised for more than 11 years. The arrest followed an investigation into a petition alleging that he obtained money by false pretence, police spokesperson SP Joshua Ukandu said in a statement on Tuesday.

Police said the petitioner, Chukwu David, alleged that Enyinnaya took ₦650,000 from him in March 2026 to help process and secure approval for street naming in Ohaozara Local Government Area. David also alleged that Enyinnaya presented himself as a lawyer with years of professional experience.

According to the police, Enyinnaya admitted during questioning that he was not a lawyer. A search of his apartment led to the recovery of items police described as exhibits, including a Nigerian Bar Association seal, barrister’s robes and wig, and a portrait of the suspect wearing legal attire. Officers also reportedly found purported LL.B. and LL.M. certificates bearing Enyinnaya’s name and that of Enugu State University of Science and Technology, as well as court judgments and legal documents, including powers of attorney and deeds of conveyance.

Police said Enyinnaya had been charged to court. Ebonyi Commissioner of Police Hope Okafor praised the officers involved and urged residents to check the credentials of people offering legal services and report suspicious activity to police.

title: 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso
summary: NDC campaign chief Ibrahim Abdulkarim urged Atiku and other opposition leaders to join the Obi-Kwankwaso alliance for 2027. He said unity could challenge the APC.
body:
Ibrahim Abdulkarim, Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, has called on former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other opposition leaders to join the alliance backing Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election. He said opposition parties and figures needed to unite behind a common platform to improve their chances against the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Abdulkarim said the coalition was taking shape within the NDC, with Obi as its presidential candidate and Kwankwaso agreeing to work with him. He argued that the alliance did not have to be formed through another party, adding that Kwankwaso had set aside his own ambition. Atiku and other opposition figures, he said, were welcome to join and bring broader national reach.

He also responded to criticism of the NDC’s campaign organisation and its relationship with support groups backing Obi. Abdulkarim rejected comparisons between the party and the Obidient movement, saying a political party should not be measured against a support group. He said more than a thousand support groups were part of the NDC.

Addressing concerns among voters that their ballots might not count, Abdulkarim said the party had developed measures to protect votes in 2027. He urged people worried about electoral integrity to support the NDC and said it would campaign peacefully across the country, including in remote areas. He added that the party intended to reassure voters before the election that their votes would be protected.

title: Lagos Assembly okays state police, demands clear power-sharing
summary: Lagos lawmakers support creating state police but want clearer state powers and federal-state responsibilities. Speaker Obasa also called for dedicated security for legislatures.
body:
The Lagos State House of Assembly has endorsed the proposed creation of state police, while calling for constitutional changes that give states clearer authority over their forces and spell out how they would work alongside federal police. Speaker Mudashiru Obasa set out the concerns on Tuesday during debate on the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, sent to state legislatures by the National Assembly.

Obasa described the proposal as progress on a long-standing demand, but said the bill did not yet resolve who would control and administer state police. He warned that leaving substantial powers with the federal government could weaken the purpose of establishing state forces. The amendment, he said, should define the functions and responsibilities of each level of policing to avoid an imbalance.

The demand for state police has continued through successive National Assemblies, from the fifth to the 10th, as governments seek ways to improve security and protect lives and property, Obasa said. State legislatures are considering the constitutional changes needed to establish a State Police Service, and nearly 25 states have expressed support, according to the material provided. Obasa commended President Bola Tinubu, National Assembly leaders and state lawmakers for advancing the process, while urging them to address outstanding concerns before it is concluded.

He also argued that legislative institutions should have dedicated security arrangements. Citing past incidents in which state legislative complexes were allegedly demolished or locked at the direction of governors, he said parliamentary police could help protect legislatures from executive interference and preserve their independence. Obasa directed the Assembly’s Clerk, Adenike Oshinowo, to formally convey the Lagos resolution to the National Assembly.

title: Fake drinks may be causing liver, kidney diseases in Ondo — NMA
