summary: Ondo’s medical association says unusual liver and kidney disease cases among young people warrant investigation. It urges tighter checks on suspected counterfeit drinks.
body:
The Ondo State chapter of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) has warned that suspected fake or adulterated beverages may be contributing to liver and kidney disease among young people. The association says doctors are encountering these conditions in age groups where they are considered uncommon, but has no confirmed count of cases linked to the drinks and says investigations are continuing.

Speaking in Akure, NMA state chairman Dr Roland Bola Arohunmolase said reported cases of liver cirrhosis among teenagers, and liver and kidney disease among people aged 22 to 30, warrant closer medical scrutiny. He identified unhealthy or adulterated beverages as a possible risk factor, while stressing that the causes of individual cases have not been established.

The association recalled earlier incidents involving suspected adulterated drinks in Odigbo and Irele, which reportedly caused at least 50 deaths, and an incident in Ilere linked to methanol consumption. It warned that methanol, an industrial chemical, can cause severe poisoning and organ damage if ingested. The NMA also said suspected counterfeit beverages may be found not only in open markets but in supermarkets, hotels, bars and other retail outlets.

The association urged the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, the Ondo State Government and other relevant agencies to carry out unannounced inspections of outlets suspected of selling counterfeit drinks. It called for unsafe products to be seized and destroyed, and for those responsible for their production or distribution to be prosecuted. It also asked manufacturers to strengthen product authentication through measures such as tamper-proof seals, holograms, unique QR codes and tracking systems.

Consumers were advised to be cautious of drinks priced well below prevailing market rates and to check seals, labels and packaging before buying. Arohunmolase urged anyone who suspects they have consumed a fake or contaminated beverage to seek medical advice promptly rather than wait for symptoms to appear.

title: ‘I will forever miss you’ – Toluwanisings’ wife breaks down in tears at night of tributes
summary: Akanbi Elizabeth mourned gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji at a tribute in Ibadan. His family says burial plans await an investigation into his death.
body:
Akanbi Elizabeth broke down in tears as she remembered her late husband, gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji, at a night of tributes in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Tuesday. Addressing mourners at Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, she spoke of the pain of losing him and asked him not to forget her and their children. “Toluwanisings, my dear husband. I will forever miss you. Please do not forget your children and me,” she said.

Relatives, friends, colleagues and associates gathered to honour the singer, known for the song “Kabiyesi Olorun Ayo.” Gospel artistes and actors, including Adeyinka Alaseyori, Esther Igbekele, Laolu Gbenjo, Akintayo Akinwande, Bidemi Olaoba, Peterson Okopi, Sarah Apekeola and Bimbo Oshin, attended. Tributes included worship, songs and personal reflections on Bolaji’s life and musical legacy.

Bolaji and Elizabeth married in September 2021 and had two daughters. He died on 15 October after slumping at his residence in Ibadan. The supplied information does not specify the year of his death.

His burial arrangements have become a point of dispute within the family, which has not settled whether he should be buried in a cemetery, at his residence or in his hometown. Relatives say arrangements should remain on hold until authorities establish the circumstances of his death. They have called for a transparent and impartial investigation and said they would continue paying mortuary costs while inquiries proceed. The family has also alleged possible foul play, citing what it described as an absence of visible mourning at the residence when seven relatives visited; that claim has not been independently established in the information provided.

title: Lagos gives residents December 31 deadline to get health insurance
summary: Lagos residents have until December 31, 2026, to obtain health insurance before enforcement begins on January 1, 2027. New plans target workers and employers.
body:
Lagos State has set December 31, 2026, as the deadline for residents to obtain health insurance, with enforcement of mandatory coverage due to begin the following day. Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu announced the timeline while launching enforcement under Executive Order EO/BOS/01 of 2024 at an event in Victoria Island attended by government officials and health-sector stakeholders.

Sanwo-Olu also unveiled the Lagos Private Health Plans, intended to extend insurance to salaried workers and corporate organisations. The plans will complement Ilera Eko, which serves vulnerable residents and people working in the informal sector. The governor said the policy requires residents, employers and workers to have social health insurance, and places responsibilities on individuals, businesses and government.

He urged employers to treat workers’ healthcare as a necessary business cost, comparable to pension obligations. Sanwo-Olu also said health providers should stabilise patients needing emergency care before addressing payment or insurance status, and should not refuse emergency treatment because of financial constraints. He said 21 health maintenance organisations had endorsed participation in the new plans, which bring government and private operators together to expand coverage.

Lagos Commissioner for Health Akin Abayomi said newer medical technologies, including artificial intelligence, robotic science and modern diagnostic equipment, had raised the cost of healthcare. He argued that insurance could help shield households from rising expenses and reduce reliance on out-of-pocket payments. Adebayo Adedewe, chairman of the Lagos State Health Management Agency, said the state had increased its Health Equity Fund from N1 billion to N3 billion, with the aim of covering more than 500,000 vulnerable residents unable to afford premiums. He said the agency would continue enrolment and public-awareness efforts through community outreach and media campaigns.

title: FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers
summary: The government approved a six-month ₦70,000 transport payment for workers from November 2026. It also agreed to settle allowance arrears, while minimum-wage talks continue.
body:
The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, starting in November 2026. The decision followed a conciliation meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on October 27 to discuss issues raised by organised labour.

The government also approved peculiar allowance arrears dating from May 1, 2026. Payments are scheduled to begin in November and be made in three equal monthly instalments. The parties did not agree on when to implement the national minimum wage, but agreed to establish a Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee and have it begin work immediately.

The meeting addressed other outstanding payments. The government said 19 months of health workers’ allowance arrears would be paid within three months from December 2026. For agricultural workers’ hazard allowances, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted beneficiary details and cost estimates for verification by the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission. That review is expected to take two weeks, after which the commission will provide an implementation template.

The commission also expects to complete updated cost estimates for an adjustment to the Consolidated Health Salary Structure within three weeks. The figures will then go to the Presidential Committee on Salaries for a decision. A request for tax relief for workers will be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory matter.

The meeting was chaired by Labour Minister Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation. It followed an earlier conciliation session on October 22. Government and labour representatives agreed to meet again after one month to review progress, and called on state and local governments to take part in the intervention process. Unions were urged to advocate for implementation at their respective levels.

title: ‘I have a duty to serve Nigeria, and I will’ — Adesina tells Tinubu
summary: Akinwumi Adesina told President Bola Tinubu he is ready to help Nigeria in any capacity, but said he is not seeking a government job. No role was announced.
body:
Former African Development Bank president Akinwumi Adesina has told President Bola Tinubu he is ready to contribute to Nigeria’s development in any capacity. He made the offer after meeting Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja on Tuesday, where he briefed the president on his decade leading the bank. Adesina said he was not seeking a government appointment, adding: “I’m not looking for a job. I’m not looking for anything. I’m just here to help.” No specific role or appointment was announced after the meeting.

Adesina said the AfDB provided about $7 billion in financing to Nigeria between 2015 and 2025, compared with $11.1 billion in cumulative financing since the bank began operating in the country in 1971. He said the amount provided during his tenure represented 63 per cent of the total. His term as AfDB president ended in 2025 after two five-year terms. He was elected in 2015 and re-elected in 2020.

An agricultural economist, Adesina served as Nigeria’s minister of agriculture and rural development from 2011 to 2015. In that role, he promoted an electronic-wallet system through which farmers could receive support for seeds and fertiliser by mobile phone. The AfDB said the programme reached 15 million farmers in its first four years. During his leadership of the bank, its agenda included expanding electricity access, improving food security and supporting industrialisation and regional integration. The bank’s general capital rose from $93 billion to $208 billion in 2019 following a shareholder decision, its largest increase at the time.

Adesina also praised Tinubu’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and the harmonisation of foreign-exchange windows. He described the measures as difficult but said signs of progress included greater foreign-exchange availability, the return of portfolio investors and a downward trend in inflation. He acknowledged, however, that prices remained high for Nigerians. Adesina said stabilising the economy was only a first step and that the country must now pursue structural transformation, growth and prosperity.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO Attracts Investors From 120 Countries, All 54 African Nations
summary: Dangote Refinery says its IPO drew applications from 120 countries, including all 54 African nations. The offer closed after attracting broad international participation.
body:
Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals says its initial public offering attracted investor applications from 120 countries, including every one of Africa’s 54 nations. The company described the response as a milestone for African capital markets, with applications spanning all six inhabited continents and extending ownership of the industrial asset to a wider group of investors.

The offer opened on September 14, with 4.1 billion ordinary shares priced at ₦525 each and a proposed capital raise of about ₦2.15 trillion. It was originally due to close on October 13, but the Securities and Exchange Commission approved an extension to October 27 to give investors more time to apply. The company said applications were available through commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital-market institutions and other distribution partners.

Aliko Dangote, president and chief executive of Dangote Industries Limited, said the participation showed that Africans wanted to invest in and own businesses producing goods on the continent. He said the IPO was intended not only to raise funds but also to widen public ownership. The company plans to continue its expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, focusing on operational performance and Africa’s energy security.

David Bird, managing director and chief executive of the refinery, said the international response reflected confidence in its scale, operations and prospects. He said the company would focus on operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value. Group Chief Financial Officer Murat Erden said the offer demonstrated how African financial institutions and digital platforms could connect investors across borders and potentially support broader retail participation and more integrated capital markets.

Erden also said the refinery recorded $22.5 billion in revenue and $5.52 billion in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation in the first nine months of 2026. The company is pursuing plans to expand its refining and petrochemical operations and strengthen distribution. Located in Lagos, the refinery was established to increase domestic processing capacity and reduce reliance on imported refined petroleum products.

title: Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police
summary: Sokoto lawmakers unanimously approved a constitutional amendment proposal for state police. The measure would divide duties between federal and state services.
body: Abdullahi said the constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the state assemblies in at least two-thirds of the states. Lawmakers who spoke in the debate supported state policing as a response to security challenges. Speaker Tukur Bala put the motion to a voice vote, and the assembly adopted it unanimously.

title: EFCC recovers additional $40 million from Nestoil, total hits $100 million
summary: EFCC has recovered another $40 million from Nestoil, bringing payments under a repayment arrangement to $100 million. Lenders say substantial debts remain outstanding.
body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has recovered an additional $40 million from Nestoil Limited, bringing total payments under a repayment arrangement to $100 million. The lenders said the latest payment was made on October 19, 2026, following an earlier $60 million payment reported in August.

The arrangement was reached at a meeting chaired by EFCC Chairman Olanipekun Olukoyede to address obligations involving Nestoil, its affiliate Neconde Energy Limited and a consortium of lenders. It sets out a framework for orderly repayment, subject to the terms agreed by the parties and applicable laws. The lenders described the latest recovery as an encouraging development, but said a substantial portion of the debt remains unpaid.

The consortium has reaffirmed its commitment to working with the EFCC and other relevant stakeholders to recover the outstanding amounts. Its members include Access Bank, Zenith Bank, Ecobank, African Export-Import Bank, First Bank of Nigeria, First City Monument Bank, United Bank for Africa and Union Bank of Nigeria.

The lenders said in June 2026 that Nestoil’s total indebtedness had reached approximately $1.084 billion and N469.43 billion. The facilities originated as bilateral loans dating back to 2010 and were consolidated under a restructuring arrangement known as the “Global Club,” which took effect in 2023. The lenders said repayment defaults continued after the restructuring.

The dispute escalated in October 2025, when a Federal High Court in Lagos granted a Mareva injunction freezing assets, bank accounts and shares linked to Nestoil, Neconde and their promoters. In June 2026, the Supreme Court set aside interim preservative orders granted by the Court of Appeal and directed the parties to return to the lower court to address the substantive issues. The lenders said that decision did not extinguish the debt or invalidate the recovery process. They say the remaining obligations are still to be settled under the repayment plan.

title: Kidnappers abduct six in Kaduna
summary: Six people were reportedly abducted from an estate in Kaduna’s Millennium City on Tuesday morning after attackers entered through a second gate and opened fire.
body:
Suspected kidnappers abducted six people during an early-morning attack on Nuru Suraj Estate in the Millennium City area of Kaduna metropolis on Tuesday. Residents were sent scrambling for safety when the assailants entered the estate and fired shots, according to accounts from the area.

A resident who identified herself as Maman Hamid said her home was close to those of the victims. She said the attackers gained access through the estate’s second gate before taking the six people to an unknown destination.

The victims’ identities and whether their families had been contacted were not clear at the time the incident was reported. The attack has added to concerns among residents about security in Millennium City, where suspected kidnappers reportedly abducted several people in another incident a few weeks earlier.

The Kaduna State Police Command had not responded to requests for comment by the time of reporting.

title: Sultan Of Sokoto To Turban Peter Igho As Kakakin Daular Usmaniyya
summary: Sultan Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III is scheduled to formally turban broadcaster Peter Igho as Kakakin Daular Usmaniyya in Sokoto on November 1, 2026.
body:
The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, is scheduled to formally turban veteran broadcaster and television producer Chief Peter Igho as Kakakin Daular Usmaniyya on Sunday, November 1, 2026. The ceremony will take place at the Sultan’s Palace in Sokoto, according to a statement from the palace.

Igho was conferred with the traditional title on September 10, 2025. The honour recognises his contributions to the development of the Sultanate Council, Sokoto State and Nigeria. The ceremony is expected to draw prominent Nigerians from across the country and from different walks of life, with the stated aim of strengthening cordial relations and promoting unity among the country’s diverse communities.

Igho is a former Executive Director at the Nigerian Television Authority and is known for producing and directing *Cock Crow at Dawn*, described as one of Nigeria’s pioneering television dramas. His work on the programme and other productions helped shape the country’s broadcasting industry. He has received national and international awards for his contributions to broadcasting and mentored generations of media professionals. A native of the Niger Delta, he is also recognised for cultural advocacy, community leadership and philanthropy.

Sultan Abubakar, who will preside over the ceremony, is the 20th occupant of the Sokoto throne and President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs. A retired Brigadier-General of the Nigerian Army, he ascended the throne on November 2, 2006, and is known for advocating peace, interfaith dialogue, education and national unity.

The Sultanate’s heritage is linked to the Sokoto Caliphate, also known as Daular Usmaniyya, founded in 1804 by Islamic scholar and reformer Shehu Usman Dan Fodio. The Sultanate Council remains a custodian of that heritage and an institution associated with Islamic leadership, peacebuilding and national cohesion in Nigeria.

title: Nasarawa Assembly decries resurgence of kidnappings
summary: Nasarawa lawmakers called for stronger security after reports of kidnappings in Lafia and nearby communities. The House urged coordinated action by state agencies and local leaders.
body:
The Nasarawa State House of Assembly has urged stronger security measures following reports of renewed kidnappings in Lafia and other parts of the state. Speaker Danladi Jatau raised the concern during Tuesday’s plenary in Lafia, responding to a matter presented by Lafia Central representative Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki.

Akwashiki told lawmakers that two people had been abducted in Agyaragu Lafia the previous day, while people were also kidnapped in Agunji Lafia a few days earlier. He said the two people taken in the more recent incident remained with their abductors, who were demanding ransom. He called on the state government and security agencies to act to protect residents and property.

Jatau said the House would treat the matter seriously, citing fear among residents and disruption to economic activity. The Assembly urged Governor Abdullahi Sule to direct security agencies, including the police, the Department of State Services and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, to strengthen efforts across the state. It also called for traditional leaders and vigilantes to work together to identify unfamiliar people in their communities.

The Speaker directed the Clerk of the House to send the resolution to the governor for action. Lawmakers who supported the motion said kidnappings were affecting their constituents and called for more decisive measures by state and federal authorities. They also urged both levels of government to procure more sophisticated weapons and deploy technology to address insecurity.

title: Ernest Shonekan Centre Launches Portal to Track Legislation Affecting Nigeria’s Business Environment
summary: A new portal will help users find and track National Assembly bills that could affect Nigerian businesses. It includes bill histories and legislative-stage analytics.
body:
The Ernest Shonekan Centre for Legislative Reforms and Economic Development has launched a digital portal for tracking proposed laws with potential implications for Nigeria’s business environment. The centre is an initiative of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG). The Business Bill Intelligence Portal was launched at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, held at the Transcorp Hilton Hotel in Abuja under the theme “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity.”

Users can browse and search bills, and apply available filters to find legislation of interest. An analytics dashboard summarises bills and shows their distribution across legislative stages. Individual bill pages provide each proposal’s status, latest recorded action and legislative history, allowing users to follow its progress.

The centre says the portal is intended to make it easier for businesses and other stakeholders to identify relevant proposals and understand their possible effects. Laws can shape investment decisions, business operations, market access, regulatory requirements and the cost of doing business, but tracking bills and determining their relevance to particular sectors can be difficult. ESC Chairman Kyari Bukar said the initiative aims to encourage informed participation in legislative reform and support laws that improve the business environment while protecting the public interest.

The portal builds on the NESG’s work with the legislature. In 2016, the group established the National Assembly Business Environment Roundtable to bring legislative and private-sector participants together on reform; it later supported the State Assemblies Business Environment Roundtable, extending dialogue to the subnational level. Established in 2023, ESC focuses on research, advocacy and engagement on legislative reform and economic development.

ESC Executive Director Uchenna Ogbonna said the portal is intended for a broad range of users, including businesses, citizens, civil society organisations, journalists, researchers, government agencies and legislators. The centre says it aims to support awareness, informed participation and dialogue on legislation affecting Nigeria’s economy. The portal is available at https://billtracker.shonekancentre.org.

title: Chelsea’s Joao Pedro ruled out with thigh injury
summary: Joao Pedro is expected to miss several weeks with a thigh injury, Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso said. Cole Palmer is also unavailable for the Liverpool match through suspension.
body:
Chelsea forward Joao Pedro is expected to be out for “a few weeks” with a thigh injury, head coach Xabi Alonso said ahead of Wednesday’s Carabao Cup match against Liverpool. The Brazilian missed Chelsea’s defeat to Tottenham because of the injury and is not ready to play in the team’s next matches. Alonso said he could not give a more precise estimate for his return.

Alonso called Joao Pedro an important player and said Chelsea would feel his absence during a demanding run of fixtures. He expressed confidence, however, that the squad had enough options to compete, with the team focused on preparing for Liverpool and finding solutions among the players available.

Chelsea will also be without Cole Palmer for the Liverpool trip. The England international was sent off against Tottenham and is unavailable through suspension. Alonso said he had discussed the incident with Palmer, who understood that the mistake could have been avoided. He said he hoped it would not happen again.

Despite the suspension, Alonso said Palmer was in a good place with his teammates and that the club wanted him to enjoy his football. The coach’s comments came as Chelsea prepared to face Liverpool without two players who will be unavailable for the cup tie.

title: Mutfwang Vows To Track Down Gero Killers, Urges Communities To Remain Vigilant
summary: Plateau Governor Caleb Mutfwang vowed to pursue Gero attackers and urged residents to report threats. Police confirmed six deaths; community representatives said seven.
body:
Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang has vowed to pursue those responsible for a deadly attack in Gero, in Jos South Local Government Area, and urged residents to share timely information with security agencies. Speaking on Tuesday at the swearing-in of Special Advisers at the New Government House in Jos, he described the attack, which occurred on Monday night, as disturbing, particularly because it was close to Jos metropolis. He said investigators had recovered evidence and were following leads.

Mutfwang urged communities across the state to remain vigilant, saying security forces relied on residents’ information to respond to threats. He also said the alleged leader of an attack on Kombun District in Mangu Local Government Area had been arrested, and that his administration would continue efforts to prosecute suspects linked to violence.

The Plateau State Police Command confirmed six deaths in Gero, revising an earlier figure of seven reported by community representatives. Police spokesperson SP Alfred Alabo said unidentified armed men opened fire in the community in the early hours of Tuesday. Mobile police and tactical officers, working with military personnel and Operation Rainbow, dislodged the attackers, who fled into nearby hillside forest. The victims’ bodies were taken to a morgue and an injured person was transported to hospital.

Alabo said joint security forces had launched search and clearance operations, which remained ongoing, and recovered motorcycles and other items allegedly abandoned by the attackers. Commissioner of Police Ayodeji Faniyan visited the community and met local leaders and residents. He called for stronger cooperation on intelligence gathering and urged people to report suspicious activity, while community representatives appealed for measures to prevent further violence and a sustained security presence.

title: Tinubu aware of food prices – Presidential aide
summary: A presidential aide says Bola Tinubu receives regular briefings on food prices, including eggs and bread. She also outlined plans for the Mokwa-Bida road.
body:
President Bola Tinubu receives regular briefings about the prices of everyday food items, including eggs and bread, according to his Senior Special Assistant on Community Engagement for the North-Central region, Dr Abiodun Essiet. Speaking to State House correspondents at the Presidential Villa in Abuja on Tuesday, Essiet said community representatives and members of the Federal Executive Council communicate information about the pressures Nigerians face. She disputed the idea that journalists alone understand those challenges.

Essiet also described infrastructure as central to the administration’s development agenda, pointing to the Mokwa-Bida road in Niger State. She said residents had repeatedly called for the route to be addressed and that a crowd gathered when she visited a section of it. According to Essiet, the road was last awarded a contract 46 years ago. She added that heavy vehicles had been involved in accidents while attempting to navigate it, and said people had died on the road.

Essiet said Tinubu had directed that the road contract be awarded with a requirement for reinforced concrete construction rather than ordinary asphalt, which she said was intended to make the work durable. She was appointed to her North-Central community engagement role in 2024. Separately, Vice President Kashim Shettima said on October 19 that food prices would fall in the coming weeks as the government responds to agricultural challenges.

title: “Advertising Brings a Player Once, Actually Paying Winners Brings Them Back” — Helabet Representative Says
summary: Helabet says it is shifting some marketing funds toward payouts, bonuses and customer support. The company is also considering sponsoring a Nigerian football club.
body:
Helabet representative Olajay says the sportsbook is redirecting some marketing spending toward player experience, arguing that advertising can attract a first-time user but service and reliable payouts influence whether that person stays. He said the company is putting more resources into bonuses, localisation, staff and operational funds intended to support prompt payment of legitimate winnings.

Olajay linked the shift to rising marketing costs, competition and compliance requirements, as well as the naira’s decline against the US dollar. He said some customer-acquisition expenses are tied to dollar costs, making a strategy based on continually increasing advertising spending difficult to sustain. Helabet plans to introduce a 305% welcome bonus, alongside a 25% daily bonus on a first deposit, a weekly rebate and a promotional-code store where players can exchange points for single or accumulator bets. The company also offers free mobile data for MTN and Glo users, which Olajay described as a Nigeria-specific feature.

The representative said regulatory changes have added complexity to operating in Nigeria. Following the late-2024 decentralisation of gaming regulation, states gained authority over the sector. Olajay said the Federation of State Gaming Regulators of Nigeria and its Universal Reciprocity Certificate allowed Helabet to operate under a unified certificate across 22 member states, rather than seeking separate licences in each. He also said the company is adjusting to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and would not compromise on compliance, including working with state regulators and meeting tax obligations.

Helabet’s stated aim is to become an operator that Nigerians recommend based on its odds, event selection, bonuses and withdrawals. Olajay said the company is considering sponsoring a Nigerian football club and has drawn up a shortlist, with negotiations expected to begin later. He presented local hiring and investment in sports as part of the company’s longer-term approach, alongside its focus on player service and regulatory compliance.

title: Foreign governments are blocking japa, Nigeria must now give its talent a reason to stay
summary: Visa restrictions in key destinations are narrowing routes for Nigerians. The analysis says better services and security are needed to encourage voluntary returns.
body:
Tighter immigration rules in several major destinations are narrowing options for Nigerian students and workers, even as some economic indicators at home improve. In Britain, the student visa refusal rate for Nigerians rose from 4.5% in the first half of 2025 to 22.7% in 2026. A lower threshold for universities’ sponsor refusal rates led some institutions to withdraw offers. Britain also raised the skills threshold for work visas and ended overseas recruitment of new care workers. The United States partially suspended immigrant visas for Nigerians from January 2026 and restricted several other visa categories, while later resuming processing for foreign-trained doctors. Canada has tightened parts of its system while creating targeted permanent-residence routes for some international doctors.

The changes are reflected in health-worker recruitment figures. In the year to March 2026, 1,614 Nigerian-trained nurses and midwives joined the UK register, down from 2,363 the previous year. Nigeria has 95,456 registered doctors, but 60,551 hold active practising licences; an estimate cited in the analysis puts the number working in the domestic health system at about 31,000. A 2025 national health report recorded 20,966 health professionals relocating abroad in one year, including 3,919 doctors and 7,487 nurses and midwives.

At the same time, some domestic indicators have improved. Inflation fell to 14.63% in September 2026, economic growth reached 4.43% in the second quarter, and personal transfers from abroad totalled $11.12 billion in the first half of the year. But electricity supply remains a major constraint: generation fell to 2,034 megawatts in an October collapse, despite installed capacity of 13,625 megawatts. The International Organization for Migration recorded 14,787 Nigerians returning with its support in 2025, though the figure does not distinguish voluntary returns from deportations or other forms of compelled return.

The analysis argues that fewer departures alone will not make return sustainable. It calls for more reliable electricity, improved security, stable economic conditions, recognition of overseas qualifications, pay that can compete for shortage occupations and better tracking of professionals. It also says people returning involuntarily should receive skills assessments and pathways into suitable work. Without such measures, the recent restrictions may reduce opportunities to leave without giving skilled Nigerians a lasting reason to build their futures at home.

title: EKO HOTELS AT 50: THE NIGHT AFRICAN HOSPITALITY STOPPED ASKING FOR A SEAT AT THE GLOBAL TABLE
summary: Eko Hotels & Suites marked its 50th anniversary with a gala in Lagos attended by more than 1,000 guests. The celebrations also included a summit on Africa’s tourism and cultural industries.
body:
Eko Hotels & Suites marked its 50th anniversary with a gala at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos on October 2, 2026. The Legacy Gala & Awards brought together more than 1,000 guests from business, government, entertainment, culture and society, including Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and Deputy Governor Kadri Obafemi Hamzat. Music performances featured Wyclef Jean and Flavour.

The anniversary programme also included the Africa Legacy Summit, held earlier in May. It brought together policymakers, scholars, diplomats, tourism professionals, business leaders, creatives and young Africans to discuss culture, hospitality, tourism and travel. Topics included investment, sustainability, innovation, youth participation and ways to translate Africa’s cultural assets into economic opportunities.

The celebrations highlighted the hotel’s development beyond accommodation, including experiences and events such as Tropical Christmas Wonderland, Theatre @ Eko Hotels and Hakuna Matata Theme Park. The anniversary material presented these activities as examples of how hospitality venues can support cultural production and encourage travel, while generating opportunities across sectors such as entertainment, transport and food services.

The event also recognised the employees whose work has sustained the hotel over five decades, from housekeeping and engineering to security, events and administration. Its leadership team includes Managing Director Ghassan Faddoul and General Manager Danny Kioupouroglou. The anniversary framed the hotel’s next phase around maintaining its relevance through continued investment in hospitality, cultural experiences and destination development.

title: No government will use Ebola as political weapon —NCDC DG
summary: NCDC Director-General Jide Idris said Ebola would not be used as a political tool. He said there is no current reason to postpone Nigeria’s 2027 elections.
body:
Nigeria’s disease-control chief, Jide Idris, said the government would not use the Ebola outbreak for political purposes. Speaking on Monday, the Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention said the health response was not being driven by electoral considerations, amid claims that disease controls could be used to influence the 2027 elections.

Asked whether the outbreak could lead to a postponement, Idris said that decision was beyond his authority. He said there was no current reason to delay the elections, while acknowledging that a widespread outbreak could raise public health concerns. The Independent National Electoral Commission has set 16 January 2027 for the presidential and National Assembly elections.

Idris said Nigerian health authorities had monitored the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo for months and had prepared for the possibility of an imported case because of population movement and international flights. Although the index patient was evacuated to Switzerland, Idris cautioned that Nigeria was not yet Ebola-free. He said there was no active positive case, but contacts were being followed up and suspected exposures investigated.

The response has also become part of political debate. African Democratic Congress presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar questioned the government’s handling of the outbreak and sought an account of N10 billion approved for preparedness. The APC Presidential Campaign Council accused him of politicising the health emergency and said the funding remained untouched. The State House announced in June that President Bola Tinubu had approved the emergency funds to strengthen NCDC preparedness and support public health response activities.

title: Morning recap: Kane wins Ballon d’Or, EFCC arrests 15, other top stories
summary: Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or as labour talks loom in Nigeria. The EFCC, Senate, courts and government revenue figures also feature in today’s updates.
body:
Harry Kane has won the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, becoming the first Englishman to receive the award since Michael Owen in 2001. The Bayern Munich striker and England captain was recognised at a ceremony at the London Palladium after what was described as a prolific season for the German club.

In Ogun State, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission arrested 14 Chinese nationals and one Nigerian at four alleged illegal lithium processing plants in Ogere. The commission said the operation followed intelligence gathering and surveillance. Investigators recovered lithium rocks, 18 mobile devices, four laptops and a trailer truck. The suspects are expected to face charges after the investigation is complete.

The Federal Government and organised labour are due to resume talks on workers’ demands, including lower petrol prices and a review of the national minimum wage. The Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress have warned that a lack of progress could lead to nationwide industrial action. Separately, a prosecution witness told a Lagos court that social media personality Blessing Okoro, known as Blessing CEO, falsely claimed ownership of a property before collecting N69.15m. The witness cited WhatsApp conversations and other documents; Okoro has pleaded not guilty, and the case remains before the court.

The Senate has pledged to pass legislation establishing state police before the end of 2026, following approval of the constitutional amendment by the required number of state assemblies. The proposed system still has legislative steps to complete. Nigeria’s statutory revenue for the first 10 months of 2026 was N20.74tn below target, despite a sharp rise in crude oil prices. Music executive Don Jazzy has also announced a 2027 scholarship programme at TS Academy, offering eligible Nigerians up to full tuition coverage for technology and digital-skills courses. Laptop and data support may be available to successful applicants, but an application fee applies.

title: CIS confab to rally capital mobilisation for infrastructure, manufacturing
summary: CIS will hold its 30th annual conference in Lagos on November 4–5, focused on financing productive investment. Sessions will address infrastructure, manufacturing and SMEs.
body:
The Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers will hold its 30th annual conference in Lagos on November 4 and 5, bringing together economic policymakers, financial market regulators, institutional investors and industry leaders. The event will focus on how to direct capital towards productive investment and support economic growth.

Under the theme “From Capital Mobilised to Prosperity Realised: Financing Nigeria’s Next Era of Growth and Global Competitiveness,” the conference will consider how money raised through the capital market can support business expansion, job creation and competitiveness. CIS President Dr Fiona Ahimie said the discussion should look beyond the amount of capital raised to how effectively it is deployed to expand productive capacity and strengthen businesses. She also identified innovation, inclusion and efficiency as important to attracting domestic and international investment.

Conference Committee Chairman Saheed Bashir said the gathering is intended to bring together participants from across the investment value chain and develop practical recommendations for financing Nigeria’s growth ambitions. Planned discussions will examine the connections between capital market development, technology, regulatory effectiveness and the funding requirements of the real economy.

A major session, titled “Financing Productive Investments in the Real Economy: Spotlight on Infrastructure, Manufacturing, and SMEs,” will focus on expanding access to long-term finance for sectors considered important to development. It will explore how capital markets can complement bank lending by linking businesses and infrastructure projects with longer-term funding from institutional and other investors. Organisers say the conference aims to produce proposals that policymakers, regulators, investors and industry leaders can put into practice.

title: Ebola: Patient Arrives Switzerland, Nigeria Continues Contact Tracing, Containment — Pate
summary: Nigeria’s Ebola index patient and her spouse arrived safely in Switzerland, where they are receiving care and isolation. Contact tracing and containment continue in Nigeria.
body:
Nigeria’s Ebola index patient and her spouse have arrived safely in Switzerland, Health and Social Welfare Minister Ali Pate said. The patient is receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals, while her husband has been placed in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. Nigerian authorities continue to monitor contacts, investigate alerts and carry out other containment measures, Pate said in an update on Monday evening.

Pate said Switzerland had thanked Nigerian health professionals for their care and recognised the cooperation between the two countries and the World Health Organisation that enabled the evacuation. He also acknowledged the work of health teams and agencies in both countries, including the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, the Swiss Federal Office of Public Health and the WHO. Africa CDC and WHO AFRO are supporting Nigeria’s continuing response.

Earlier on Monday, Pate said the patient had left Abuja with his approval. He described her as clinically much improved, stable, conscious and able to communicate, with laboratory results approaching baseline levels. He cautioned that improvement did not necessarily mean she was no longer infectious, and said strict public health protocols were followed during the evacuation.

Nigeria confirmed its first imported Ebola virus disease case in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, after the patient had travelled from Uganda. The infection was identified as the Bundibugyo strain. Authorities activated contact tracing, surveillance and monitoring after confirmation. Initial government information put the number of identified contacts at 44; a later WHO update said 52 people were being monitored in Nigeria, in addition to the patient’s husband. Pate said further updates would come through the NCDC and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare.

title: 2027: CJN warns judges against pressure, conflicting orders
summary: Nigeria’s chief justice urged court leaders to guard against forum shopping and conflicting orders ahead of 2027. She also called for faster, fairer justice.
body:
Chief Justice of Nigeria Kudirat Kekere-Ekun has urged heads of courts to guard against forum shopping, concealed related proceedings and efforts to secure conflicting orders ahead of the 2027 general elections. She spoke in Abuja on Monday at the opening of the 2026 Roundtable for Heads of Courts, organised by the National Judicial Institute.

Kekere-Ekun said election disputes bring intense public interest and pressure, but judges must decide politically sensitive cases impartially and according to the Constitution, the Electoral Act and court rules. She called on court leaders to put administrative arrangements in place for the orderly and timely handling of election cases. Judges, she said, should scrutinise applications, require full disclosure of relevant facts and consider related proceedings, while resisting the misuse of urgent applications or ex parte orders to gain an advantage.

She warned that forum shopping weakens consistency, encourages abuse of court processes and can damage public confidence. No litigant, she said, should be allowed to manipulate the system in search of a favourable decision. The chief justice also identified delays as a major challenge, noting that they impose financial and emotional costs on litigants and can reduce the value of judicial remedies. She urged heads of courts to review their dockets, identify long-pending cases and address avoidable delays through better scheduling, case monitoring and fewer unnecessary adjournments. She cautioned that efficiency should not be measured only by the number of cases resolved: fair hearings and competent decisions must be protected.

Kekere-Ekun also called for transparent, merit-based judicial appointments and urged court leaders to resist external pressure. She directed them to ensure judges start sittings on time and that lawyers and litigants are notified promptly when sessions are cancelled. She said courtrooms should remain professional environments where litigants are treated with dignity and lawyers with courtesy. The CJN further called for investment in judicial support staff and structured mentorship for newly appointed judges. Earlier, NJI Administrator and retired National Industrial Court President Babatunde Adejumo said the roundtable gives heads of courts an opportunity to discuss shared challenges and develop solutions, while noting that the judiciary operates under sustained public scrutiny.

title: [UPDATED] Kane Edges Yamal, Mbappe To Taste Ballon d’Or Glory
summary: Harry Kane won the men’s Ballon d’Or in London after scoring 73 goals last season. Alexia Putellas claimed her third women’s award.
body:
Harry Kane won the men’s Ballon d’Or at a ceremony in London on Monday, becoming England’s first recipient in 25 years. The Bayern Munich forward scored 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country last season, helping the German side win a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

Kane thanked his Bayern teammates for pushing him and said the move to the club had helped him reach another level. Since joining in 2023, his medals have come from domestic success in Germany. Before that, he had lost the 2019 Champions League final with Tottenham and two European Championship finals with England. He beat Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to the award; both had strong seasons, but neither won the top prize.

Alexia Putellas took the women’s Ballon d’Or for a third time. The Barcelona player was recognised for her part in the club’s Champions League win last season, before moving to London City Lionesses. Her return to the top followed an anterior cruciate ligament injury four years ago. Putellas succeeds Spain teammate Aitana Bonmatí, who was sidelined for much of last season with a leg break.

Yamal, a Barcelona winger, won the young talent award for the third consecutive time but missed out on becoming the youngest Ballon d’Or winner. Spain coach Luis de la Fuente was named men’s coach of the year, while Barcelona’s Pere Romeu received the women’s coaching award. Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for humanitarian work. Paris Saint-Germain, despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, received the men’s club of the year honour but no main individual awards. Unai Simón and Cata Coll were named the top men’s and women’s goalkeepers.

The event was the first Ballon d’Or ceremony held in England. Traffic in London delayed its start by nearly an hour, with many attendees arriving late.

title: Breaking: Harry Kane crowned 2026 Ballon d’Or winner
summary: Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or after an outstanding year with Bayern Munich and England. He beat contenders including Dembélé, Mbappé and Yamal.
body:
England captain Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, football’s leading individual award. The Bayern Munich striker received the honour at a ceremony on Monday, October 26, following a strong year for club and country.

Kane’s award recognises his performances for Bayern and the England national team. He has combined goalscoring with creating chances for teammates, establishing himself as one of the world’s leading forwards.

He prevailed over a field that included Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembélé, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal. The Ballon d’Or, organised by France Football, recognises the best footballer over the relevant assessment period. Kane’s win adds to a career in which he has become England’s all-time leading goalscorer and one of Europe’s most prolific strikers.

title: AIICO sustains retirement income for 28,000 retirees
summary: AIICO says it paid N68.1bn in claims and benefits in 2025 and provides regular retirement income to more than 28,000 annuitants across Nigeria.
body:
AIICO Insurance Plc said it paid N68.1bn in claims and benefits in 2025 and currently provides regular retirement income to more than 28,000 annuitants across Nigeria. The figures were disclosed at the company’s 2026 Annuitants Forum, which focused on retirement security, wellbeing and life after formal employment. AIICO said it pays about N2.1bn in annuity benefits each month, or approximately N25bn over the preceding 12 months.

Held under the theme “Still More to Live: Embracing Life Beyond Retirement,” the forum brought together annuitants, company management and staff. It also gave customers an opportunity to describe their experiences, raise questions about retirement income and offer feedback on the insurer’s services.

AIICO Executive Director for Retail Business, Gbenga Ilori, said the company sought to maintain relationships with retirees beyond the payment of benefits, describing its role as a long-term partnership. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Babatunde Fajemirokun characterised retirement as a new stage of life, and said annuity income can help retirees and their families meet needs such as rent, medication and school fees.

Attendee Josephine Igbinedion, a retired Nigerian Postal Authority employee, praised the timeliness of payments and the assistance available from AIICO. Dimeji Shoji, who had moved from programmed withdrawal to annuity and was attending his first forum, said the explanations at the event addressed some of his concerns about inflation.

Fajemirokun also encouraged retirees to look after their health, maintain family and social connections, continue learning and pass on their experience to younger generations. AIICO said the forum was part of its effort to stay engaged with annuitants and support their financial security and wellbeing in retirement.

title: Diri unveils AI robotic tutors in Bayelsa medical university
summary: Bayelsa Governor Douye Diri unveiled AI-powered robotic tutors at BMU with its 2025–2029 plan. He said technology should support, not replace, classroom teaching.
body:
Bayelsa Governor Douye Diri has unveiled AI-powered robotic tutors and other digital learning initiatives at Bayelsa Medical University (BMU) in Yenagoa. The unveiling took place alongside the university’s 2025–2029 Strategic Plan as part of efforts to advance medical education, research and technology in the state.

Diri said the tools should make learning more interactive and improve teaching, learning and research, while complementing rather than replacing classroom instruction and lecturers’ mentorship. He challenged the university’s management to turn the strategic plan into measurable gains in academic standards, research, infrastructure and graduate quality. He also reaffirmed state support for BMU’s ASPIRE Agenda, which includes academic excellence, sustainability, partnerships and engagement, innovation and technology, and research.

Vice-Chancellor Dimie Ogoina said the university aims to become a globally recognised institution for medical education, research and innovation. He reported that BMU had secured accreditation for nine academic programmes and that its nursing science students achieved a 96 per cent pass rate in professional examinations. The university has also established a virtual reality, artificial intelligence and mixed-reality studio, expanded digital connectivity and introduced an application for confidential communication between students, staff and university leadership. It is pursuing plans for a smart campus and centres focused on digital health, biomedical innovation, and health, environment and development.

Diri urged BMU to work with the state Ministries of Education and Health to deliver its objectives. He said the Sampou campus was nearing completion and would provide room for expansion. During his visit, he also inspected the newly established teaching hospital, which he said had facilities for X-rays and advanced scans, including CT scans. He said these services could improve access to specialised diagnostics and reduce the need for residents to travel outside Bayelsa for some procedures.

title: De la Fuente Wins Men’s Ballon d’Or Coach Of The Year
summary: Luis de la Fuente won the men’s Ballon d’Or coaching award after leading Spain to the World Cup title. Barcelona’s Pere Romeu won the women’s award.
body:
Luis de la Fuente received the Ballon d’Or men’s coach of the year award at a ceremony in London on Monday, following Spain’s World Cup victory. He credited the team’s success to players who put collective goals first and said the honour recognised work carried out over many years.

De la Fuente, 65, built his career through Spain’s national coaching system rather than as a former star player. After a playing career and a less successful period in club coaching, he applied in 2013 for a youth-team position advertised by the Spanish Football Federation. He began with the Under-19s, and some players from that group later featured in teams he led to the Nations League, Euro 2024 and World Cup titles.

Spain’s route to the World Cup trophy included a goalless draw with tournament debutants Cape Verde in its opening match. The team gained momentum and beat France 2-0 in the semi-final. In a close final against Lionel Messi’s Argentina in New Jersey, Spain held firm against physical opposition before Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in a 1-0 victory.

De la Fuente said Spanish football’s coaching and youth development provide a model for building future success. The women’s coach of the year award also went to a Spaniard: Barcelona’s Pere Romeu, recognised after leading the club to the Spanish league, Spanish cup, Super Cup and Champions League titles in one season.

title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Full top 10 ranking as Harry Kane claims award
summary: Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal. Rodri and Lionel Messi rounded out the top five.
body:
Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, finishing first in a ranking that included some of football’s leading players. The Bayern Munich striker claimed the individual award ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, who placed second and third respectively.

Manchester City midfielder Rodri took fourth place, followed by Lionel Messi in fifth. Paris Saint-Germain forward Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ranked sixth, with his teammate Ousmane Dembélé in seventh.

Erling Haaland, a striker for Manchester City, finished eighth. Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise was ninth, and Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabián Ruiz completed the top 10 in tenth place.

Kane’s win puts him ahead of a field that includes established award winners and players from the current generation. The final ranking placed contenders from Bayern Munich, Manchester City, Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona among the leading positions.

title: FG considers law to prevent reversal of economic reforms
summary: Nigeria is considering legislation to anchor a long-term economic policy framework and limit reversals by future governments. The proposal remains a consultation draft.
body:
The Federal Government is considering legislation to protect economic reforms from reversal by future administrations. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele announced the proposal at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, saying the government was seeking national agreement on principles to guide decisions on taxation, tariffs, subsidies, investment and industrial development.

The proposed Nigeria Economic Policy Framework is still a consultation draft and has not been approved as government policy. Public consultation is due to continue until November 27, 2026, after which the document is to go to the Federal Executive Council for approval and the National Economic Council for endorsement. Oyedele said the framework could also guide public officials and political appointees, potentially forming part of screening for government appointments and accompanying appointment letters.

The draft proposes mandatory Policy Impact Assessments before major economic interventions, requiring regulators to set out evidence, costs, beneficiaries and expected duration. It also recommends an annual National Economic Scorecard, published by Independence Day, to track real wages, productive employment and poverty. The framework’s stated pillars include stability, productivity, enterprise, capital, people, markets and institutions, with private businesses expected to drive growth under predictable rules.

Oyedele argued that policy uncertainty discourages investment and said future administrations should not abandon reforms for short-term political reasons, particularly the removal of petrol subsidies. He also called for temporary, performance-based protection for domestic industries, alongside stronger electricity, logistics and manufacturing competitiveness. The minister said the government was targeting low single-digit inflation before the end of 2027, while declining to set a firm timetable for lower borrowing costs.

Other summit speakers stressed the need to sustain macroeconomic stability while ensuring reforms produce jobs and improvements in household welfare. Anambra Governor Charles Soludo said growth of about four per cent was insufficient for rapid poverty reduction and employment creation. Participants also highlighted infrastructure, electricity, logistics and export development as priorities for raising productivity and competitiveness.

title: Evacuated Ebola patient, husband arrive in Switzerland
summary: A woman receiving treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease and her husband arrived in Switzerland after evacuation from Abuja. Nigeria continues to monitor contacts.
body:
Nigeria’s Ebola patient and her husband arrived safely in Switzerland on Monday after a medical evacuation from Abuja, according to Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate. The woman is receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals. Her husband, identified as a close contact, is in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. Swiss authorities confirmed that both are Swiss citizens and said the woman is being treated for Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola.

The Swiss Federal Office of Public Health said the hospitals have facilities and trained personnel to manage the cases safely, and that the arrangements pose no public health risk in Switzerland. Pate said Swiss Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider thanked Nigerian doctors, health professionals and authorities during a telephone conversation, and expressed appreciation for cooperation between Nigeria, Switzerland and the World Health Organization. Pate also thanked the teams and agencies involved, including the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, the WHO and Swiss health authorities.

Nigeria’s response is continuing despite the patient’s evacuation. Pate said contact monitoring, investigation of alerts and other containment measures remain under way, with support from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and the WHO Regional Office for Africa. The WHO said Nigeria was monitoring 52 contacts; the NCDC had previously identified 53 primary contacts, including the patient’s husband, healthcare workers, domestic staff and people involved in collecting samples. Authorities are monitoring contacts for symptoms. The WHO said Nigeria had no active confirmed Ebola cases following the evacuation, while Switzerland had taken responsibility for the patient’s care and was monitoring her husband.

Nigeria confirmed its first case on 20 October, after a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja tested positive. She had returned from Uganda on 3 October and developed symptoms a few days later before being admitted for treatment in isolation. Pate had said Nigeria could declare the outbreak over as early as 7 December if no further confirmed or probable cases were detected.

title: Ballon d’Or: Yamal edges Cubarsi, wins Kopa Trophy 3rd time in a row
summary: Lamine Yamal won the men’s Young Talent of the Year award for a third consecutive year. He said he thought Barcelona teammate Pau Cubarsí deserved it.
body:
Barcelona and Spain forward Lamine Yamal has won the men’s Young Talent of the Year award for the third consecutive year. After receiving the honour, he expressed gratitude and said he believed his Barcelona teammate Pau Cubarsí deserved to win instead.

The 19-year-old thanked teammates at both club and international level, recognising their contributions to his success. Yamal has continued to earn recognition for his performances for Barcelona and Spain, establishing himself as one of football’s most prominent young players.

The award was presented ahead of the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony at London’s Palladium, where footballers from clubs around the world and journalists gathered for the event’s 70th edition. Harry Kane was tipped as a favourite to become England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years, with Yamal and Kylian Mbappé among his competition. The 2026 ceremony is the first time the showpiece has been held outside France.

title: [UPDATED] Ebola: Nigeria Has 54 Primary Contacts Now, Many Are In Quarantine, Says NCDC
summary: Nigeria has identified 54 primary contacts linked to the confirmed Ebola case, with most in quarantine. Three people retested after health changes were negative.
body:
Nigeria has identified 54 primary contacts linked to its confirmed Ebola case, after tracing an e-hailing driver who transported the patient to a hospital, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said. The agency had previously reported 53 contacts. Its Director-General, Jide Idris, said the additional contact was identified after officials received new information about the patient’s journey.

Idris said about 40 of the contacts were in quarantine, while six people assessed as being at lower risk were self-quarantining at home. They are being contacted and having their temperatures checked in the morning and evening. Three people who had changes in their health and were tested again were negative, he said. The NCDC is continuing to identify secondary contacts and says monitoring must be completed before it can determine that the outbreak risk has passed.

The Federal Government announced Nigeria’s first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain on October 20, 2026. The patient was a woman who had travelled to Uganda and returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7. The Ugandan authorities denied reports of an Ebola outbreak in the country. The health minister said the patient had been flown to Switzerland in a stable and conscious condition and had clinically improved. Idris said the Swiss government arranged the air ambulance following a diplomatic request, and rejected the suggestion that the transfer reflected a lack of confidence in Nigeria’s health system. He said the country had infectious-disease specialists and had brought in Nigerians with experience treating Ebola cases in 2014.

Idris said anyone experiencing symptoms, or concerned about someone who is ill, should contact a public health centre or call the NCDC’s toll-free hotline at 6232, which he said is staffed around the clock. Nigeria has no active positive case, but the agency is continuing to follow contacts and conduct testing.

title: OAU announces resumption date for 2026/2027 session
summary: Obafemi Awolowo University has set November 1, 2026, for new students to resume, with lectures for the new session due to begin on November 16.
body:
Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU) has announced the schedule for the start of its 2026/2027 academic session. Newly admitted students are expected to arrive on campus on Sunday, November 1, while online registration is scheduled to open the following day, according to the university’s management.

Orientation for new students will run from November 2 to 6. The programme is intended to introduce them to the university’s academic environment, rules, traditions and expectations, and help prepare them for university life.

The university has also scheduled ICT training for the new students from November 9 to 13. The training will cover essential digital skills and familiarise students with the ICT facilities and platforms used to support their academic activities.

Returning undergraduates are expected back on campus on Sunday, November 15. Lectures are due to begin on Monday, November 16. Management urged new and returning students to follow the schedule and asked parents, guardians and other stakeholders to support the start of the session. Vice-Chancellor Simeon Bamire wished students a safe return and a productive academic year.

title: NGX rallies as equity market cap reaches record N163.1 trillion
summary: The NGX’s market value rose N2.64 trillion to a record N163.16 trillion on Monday. The All-Share Index also set a high, led by industrial shares.
body:
The Nigerian Exchange’s equity market capitalisation rose by N2.64 trillion on Monday, October 26, to a record N163.16 trillion. It had closed at N160.52 trillion on Friday, October 23. Monday’s total also surpassed the previous record of N163.06 trillion, set on September 23.

The NGX All-Share Index gained 4,068.27 points, or 1.65%, to close at a record 251,290.54 points, up from 247,222.27 in the previous session. The market’s advance came as gains in industrial and banking shares outweighed losses in some individual stocks.

The strongest sector move came from the NGX Industrial Index, which climbed 5.37% to 11,218.05 points from 10,646.68. Dangote Cement was a key driver, rising by the maximum permitted 10% for the session. Its share price added N111.10 to close at N1,222.10, lifting the company’s market capitalisation to N20.62 trillion.

Other sectors also advanced. The NGX Oil/Gas Index rose 0.88% to 6,089.08 points, supported by a 2.48% gain in Aradel Holdings, which closed at N1,439.90. The Insurance Index added 0.67% to reach 1,056.47 points, with AIICO Insurance up 4.18% and Coronation Insurance gaining 2.88%. Profit-taking weighed on some stocks, including ABC Transport, down 9.59%, and Caverton Offshore Support Group, down 9.38%. Select consumer-facing and specialised segments also recorded mild pullbacks.

title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Full list of winners as rankings revealed
summary: The 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings are being announced live in London, with five men’s-category places from 25th to 29th revealed. The overall winner has not yet been named.
body:
The 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings are being unveiled during a ceremony in London on Monday, October 26. The positions announced so far include five players placed between 25th and 29th in the men’s category.

Paris Saint-Germain captain Marquinhos is ranked 25th, followed by Bayern Munich defender Dayot Upamecano in 26th. Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes is 27th, Al-Qadsiah forward Julian Quiñones is 28th, and Arsenal defender William Saliba shares 29th place.

The rankings are being released as the ceremony proceeds. The supplied announcements do not yet identify the eventual winner or the players in the highest positions. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is among the leading contenders, alongside Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal and other leading players.

The award recognises individual performances over the relevant assessment period, considering players’ performances, achievements and overall contribution to football.

title: Report online sellers who deliver wrong items, Lagos tells consumers
summary: Lagos’ consumer agency urged residents to report online sellers who deliver goods unlike those ordered or below promised quality. Complaints can be filed with LASCOPA.
body:
The Lagos State Government has urged consumers to report online sellers who deliver products that differ from what customers ordered or fail to meet the quality promised. The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) issued the advice in a consumer awareness message on Monday, saying residents should speak up about such purchases rather than remain silent.

The agency said goods bought online should match their descriptions and orders. It encouraged affected consumers to take action when vendors fail to fulfil their obligations, identifying such cases as potential unfair business practices.

LASCOPA asked consumers to register complaints with the agency. It provided the toll-free helpline 080 0005 2726 for people seeking to report concerns. The agency also reaffirmed its commitment to consumer rights in Lagos State.

title: Ebola: Resident doctors demand urgent hospital preparedness, protection of frontline workers
summary: Resident doctors have been told to check hospitals’ Ebola readiness, protective equipment and referral systems. NARD wants preliminary reports within 72 hours.
body:
The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has directed members nationwide to assess hospitals’ readiness to identify and manage suspected Ebola cases and ensure frontline staff have appropriate protective equipment. The instruction was issued in a circular dated 26 October, after Nigeria confirmed an imported Ebola case on 20 October.

NARD said resident doctors can face occupational exposure because they often assess patients whose febrile illnesses have not yet been diagnosed. It asked members to work with hospital management and infection prevention and control committees to review procedures for identifying, isolating and safely referring suspected cases.

The association also called for checks on the availability and accessibility of personal protective equipment, particularly in emergency, internal medicine, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, and other high-risk departments. Hospitals were asked to hold immediate staff sessions on NCDC case definitions, infection prevention, protective equipment use and occupational exposure protocols. Resident doctors should also know the reporting channels, designated surveillance officers and approved isolation and referral pathways.

Each centre is to appoint an Ebola preparedness focal person and submit a preliminary report to NARD’s national secretariat within 72 hours of receiving the circular. Reports should describe preparedness, available equipment, gaps and urgent needs. Members were also told to raise concerns about inadequate equipment, unsafe deployment or exposure through hospital safety structures. NARD’s national officers plan to engage the NCDC, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and other stakeholders on training and occupational protection.

The case involved a 42-year-old woman who returned from Uganda via Addis Ababa on 3 October and later sought care at private facilities in Abuja. The NCDC was notified on 19 October, and tests confirmed Ebola the next day. The health minister said she was medically evacuated to Switzerland with her asymptomatic husband and was stable and clinically improved before the transfer. The WHO’s regional director for Africa subsequently said Nigeria had no active Ebola case, while stressing the importance of contact tracing and other public health measures.

title: ‘Atiku majored in hygiene, cannot rule Nigeria’s modern economy’ — Shettima
summary: Kashim Shettima criticised Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy, questioning his ability to manage the economy. Subsidy policy remains contested.
body:
‘Atiku majored in hygiene, cannot rule Nigeria’s modern economy’ — Shettima

Vice President Kashim Shettima criticised former vice president Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy, arguing it would take Nigeria back towards poverty. Shettima made the remarks at the Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Monday, accusing Atiku of supporting the policy for political convenience.

“One of the leading presidential candidates is advocating for the return of the subsidy scheme. He wants us to backslide into penury for political convenience,” Shettima said. He also challenged Atiku’s suitability to govern, referring to his training at the Kano School of Hygiene and saying he lacked the skill set to manage a modern economy.

Shettima further questioned Atiku’s knowledge of environmental sanitation, saying he did not think the former vice president could distinguish between flu and Ebola. He urged Nigerians to weigh political leaders’ proposals and qualifications before making decisions, warning those at the summit not to “play the ostrich.”

Atiku has advocated restoring the subsidy as part of his proposed approach to managing the economy. The issue remains a point of disagreement between the opposition and the administration of President Bola Tinubu, which removed the subsidy in May 2023. The government has defended the decision as necessary to reduce pressure on public finances, while the removal has been accompanied by higher fuel prices and increased living costs for many Nigerians.

title: Nollywood shoots up to 90% of films without proper script development – MBO Capital
summary: An MBO Capital executive estimates that 80% to 90% of Nollywood films start production without adequate script development. He says debt-focused financing leaves little funding for early creative work.
body:
An estimated 80% to 90% of Nollywood films move into production without adequate script development, according to Adekunle Adebiyi, executive director of investments at MBO Capital Management. Speaking in an interview on Drinks and Mics, he said Nigeria produces about 2,500 films each year, with many progressing from a first screenplay draft directly to filming.

Adebiyi attributed the pattern to the industry’s reliance on debt financing, which generally covers production and post-production rather than earlier creative work. He said script development requires equity investment because there is no certainty about when, or whether, the money put into a screenplay will be recovered. MBO Capital’s film investments have mainly used debt to fund production, post-production and, in some cases, marketing.

He cited Call of My Life, which he described as the year’s highest-grossing Nigerian film, as an example of the firm’s role in financing. MBO Capital supported its international marketing rather than its production. Adebiyi argued that access to more patient equity capital could give filmmakers time to develop stories and characters before filming begins.

He also pointed to uncertainty around distribution and revenue recovery as a barrier to investment. Investors may struggle to determine how and when they will recoup their capital, particularly when producers rely on streaming platforms to acquire films. A limited number of cinemas in Nigeria also restricts potential revenue, he said.

MBO Capital assesses film proposals against a framework of approximately 10 to 12 criteria. Despite the financing and distribution challenges, Adebiyi said investor interest remained significant, with the firm receiving at least one film-financing proposal each day. Nollywood’s production volume is high, but access to structured financing remains a constraint for filmmakers.

title: Yobe activates emergency response over Ebola, assures residents
summary: Yobe has activated its emergency system after Nigeria confirmed an imported Ebola case. Officials say the state has no cases and are stepping up preparedness.
body:
Yobe activates emergency response over Ebola, says state has no cases

Yobe State has activated its public health emergency response system after Nigeria confirmed an imported case of Ebola virus disease. At a briefing in Damaturu on Monday, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health and Human Services Hadiza Sabo said no cases had been recorded in Yobe.

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed the case on October 20, 2026. Sabo said the patient is a diplomat who travelled from Uganda and tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain. The patient is in isolation and receiving care, while the NCDC has activated its national incident management system. As of October 24, 53 close contacts, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel-related contacts, were being monitored. Forty-six exposed people had also been placed on a 21-day no-fly list as a precaution.

Sabo said the NCDC had assessed the risk of Ebola importation as high, citing regional transmission, international travel and porous borders. However, she said there was no evidence of community transmission in Nigeria. Governor Mai Mala Buni has directed the activation of Yobe’s emergency incident management system and the preparation of a state response plan, she added.
