title: Ebola: Lagos Intensifies Surveillance, Reassures Residents Of Preparedness
summary: Lagos reports no suspected Ebola cases. It is strengthening surveillance after Nigeria confirmed its first Bundibugyo virus case.
body:
The Lagos State Government says there are currently no suspected Ebola cases in the state and that it is strengthening surveillance and response preparations. The measures follow confirmation of Nigeria’s first case of the Bundibugyo virus in the Federal Capital Territory. The state urged residents and visitors to remain calm and rely on official information.

Through the Ministry of Health’s Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, Lagos is increasing disease monitoring, public communication and community engagement. It is also working with agencies at points of entry, including Murtala Muhammed International Airport. A recent engagement at the airport involved its management, Port Health Services and other aviation and public health stakeholders, with discussions covering passenger screening, information sharing, infection prevention and emergency coordination.

The state is distributing information about Ebola symptoms, transmission and prevention. It says the disease is mainly spread through direct contact with the blood or other body fluids of a symptomatic infected person, contaminated materials or the bodies of people who have died from the disease. Contact with infected animals can also result in infection. Symptoms may appear between two and 21 days after exposure and include fever, weakness, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain; unexplained bleeding or bruising may occur in some cases.

Because early symptoms can resemble malaria and other common illnesses, the government advises people who feel unwell, particularly after possible exposure or travel from an area with active transmission, to seek prompt medical assessment. Under Lagos’s fever-management policy, a person with fever should have a malaria rapid diagnostic test before taking antimalarial medicines. Anyone concerned about possible Ebola exposure is urged to contact public health authorities before going to a healthcare facility. In Lagos, concerns can be reported through emergency numbers 112 or 767, or to the state health ministry’s directorate at 0802 316 9485. The state says it will continue monitoring developments and coordinating its preparedness efforts.

title: Police Probe Fatal Shooting Of Two Officers In Kogi
summary: Kogi police are investigating the deaths of two officers in a shooting at ASCO Camp, Ajaokuta. The case has been referred to the state criminal investigations department.
body:
The Kogi State Police Command has opened an investigation into a fatal shooting at ASCO Camp in Ajaokuta that left two serving officers dead. Police said the incident was reported at 11:04 p.m. and that the Divisional Police Officer for Ajaokuta led officers to the scene.

According to the command’s preliminary findings, Corporal Amos Yusuf, who was on night duty, shot his colleague, Corporal Grace Onimisi, and then shot himself. Both officers were taken to separate medical facilities, where they were pronounced dead. Their remains were placed in the mortuary at ASCO Hospital. Police said an AK-47 rifle and four spent cartridges were recovered at the scene.

The case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for further inquiries. Police said the circumstances and motive remain under investigation and that the command would not speculate about details that have not been established. The commissioner of police expressed condolences to the officers’ families, colleagues and loved ones; the command said it would issue verified updates as appropriate.

He says he also received 12 awards and was the college’s salutatorian, describing the result as the fulfilment of a goal he had set for himself as a child.

In a post on X, Jaja said the scholarship followed a performance at an event in December 2017. It was intended to fund his education through secondary school and university. A report published by Tribune that month said former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike awarded him a ₦40 million scholarship after he sang at a thanksgiving service in Port Harcourt.

Jaja said the support encouraged him to pursue academic achievement while retaining his ambition to become an R&B and soul artiste. He reported earning a 5.00 GPA in eight of his ten university semesters, with scores of 4.96 and 4.87 in the other two. Across his studies, he said, he received 69 As and two Bs, while also holding several leadership positions. He added that he had been the best Arts student in secondary school.

Jaja credited his family, friends and lecturers for supporting him, and said music by singer Tems helped him stay emotionally grounded. He also described himself as the first male student to achieve the College of Law distinction. His account highlights the role the state-funded award played in enabling his education, while his academic record and honours mark the outcome of his studies at ABUAD.
